anchors.name: S&C Electric Company
anchors.site: 6601 N. Ridge Blvd., Chicago, IL 60626
anchors.evidenceScale: S&C reports about 2,000 team members at its Chicago location and headquarters in Rogers Park for 100+ years.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Direct jobs; advanced manufacturing; supplier/contractor spend; employee-owned wealth-building
anchors.rationale: Most grounded company-level anchor in Rogers Park. The multiplier is driven less by retail foot traffic and more by stable payroll, skilled manufacturing jobs, supplier demand, maintenance/logistics contracts, and employee ownership.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm percent of employees living in Rogers Park / adjacent North Side; estimate annual local vendor spend and apprenticeship/hiring pipeline.

anchors.name: Loyola University Chicago – Lake Shore Campus
anchors.site: Lake Shore Campus, Rogers Park / Edgewater
anchors.evidenceScale: Loyola reports $3B statewide annual economic impact, $1.7B within Chicago, 13,500+ supported jobs statewide, 4,000+ employees across campuses, and $343M student/visitor spending in Illinois.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Payroll; student/visitor spending; university procurement; capital projects; workforce development
anchors.rationale: Strong institutional multiplier through students, faculty/staff, families, events, research, campus services, and neighborhood-facing retail demand. The key question is how much of Loyola's citywide economic activity is retained inside Rogers Park versus leaking to Edgewater, downtown, or regional vendors.
anchors.validationNeeded: Split Lake Shore campus employment/spend from university-wide totals; quantify spending captured by Rogers Park businesses.

anchors.name: Devon Avenue / West Ridge commercial corridor
anchors.site: Devon Avenue and surrounding West Ridge business district
anchors.evidenceScale: West Ridge Chamber serves more than 200 businesses, schools, nonprofits, and residents; Devon Avenue is widely marketed as a South Asian and immigrant food/retail corridor.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Independent retail/restaurant recirculation; foot traffic; immigrant entrepreneurship; local B2B purchasing
anchors.rationale: This is a cluster rather than one company, but it is likely West Ridge's strongest local-retention engine because spending is dispersed across many independent restaurants, grocers, retailers, service firms, and family-owned enterprises.
anchors.validationNeeded: Identify the largest individual employers inside the corridor; measure vacancy, merchant sales, local ownership, and local vendor networks.

anchors.name: Misericordia Heart of Mercy
anchors.type: Nonprofit health and residential care institution
anchors.site: 6300 N. Ridge Ave., Chicago, IL 60660
anchors.evidenceScale: Misericordia supports more than 650 children and adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities; public LinkedIn profile lists 501–1,000 employees at its Chicago headquarters.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Direct care jobs; nonprofit payroll; essential human services; volunteer/family/event traffic; mission-driven reinvestment
anchors.rationale: Misericordia is the clearest single institutional employer in West Ridge. Its multiplier is anchored in care-sector employment, essential services, local family/volunteer traffic, and nonprofit reinvestment rather than commercial tourism.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm current on-site employee count and local-resident hiring share; quantify local procurement from West Ridge vendors.

anchors.name: Harry S Truman College
anchors.site: 1145 W. Wilson Ave., Chicago, IL 60640
anchors.evidenceScale: DataUSA reports $27.4M in 2023 salary expenditures; City Colleges publishes current salary data and Truman is located at 1145 W. Wilson Ave.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Payroll; student spending; workforce training; adult education; public investment
anchors.rationale: Truman is Uptown's strongest workforce-development anchor. It creates a durable daily population, provides upward-mobility pathways, and can connect residents to careers in education, health, and human services.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm current headcount by full-time/part-time status; determine how much student and vendor spending remains in Uptown.

anchors.name: Uptown entertainment district: Aragon, Riviera, Green Mill, related venues
anchors.site: Broadway/Lawrence entertainment district and surrounding Uptown venues
anchors.evidenceScale: Choose Chicago lists Aragon capacity at up to 4,500 spectators; WBEZ describes Uptown as a live music hub with the Riv, Aragon, and Green Mill.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Visitor spending; hospitality jobs; event vendors; restaurants/bars spillover; cultural tourism
anchors.rationale: The entertainment district imports non-local dollars into Uptown. Its multiplier depends on how well venues push visitors into local restaurants, bars, parking, retail, and independent businesses before and after events.
anchors.validationNeeded: Estimate annual event attendance, local vendor share, and visitor spend captured by Uptown businesses.

anchors.name: Endeavor Health Swedish Hospital
anchors.site: 5140 N. California Ave., Chicago, IL 60625
anchors.evidenceScale: Endeavor lists Swedish Hospital at 5140 N. California; the Lincoln Square chamber describes Swedish as a comprehensive health and wellness provider serving the north and northwest sides for 130+ years.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Hospital payroll; clinical jobs; patient/visitor traffic; health-service retention; supplier/maintenance contracts
anchors.rationale: Swedish is the largest likely employer and essential-service anchor in Lincoln Square. The multiplier is strongest through stable health-care payroll, patient visits, support services, and medical office/vendor demand.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm current on-campus employee count; quantify procurement and nearby business spillover from patients, visitors, and staff.

anchors.name: Old Town School of Folk Music / Lincoln Square cultural corridor
anchors.site: 4544 and 4545 N. Lincoln Ave., Chicago, IL 60625
anchors.evidenceScale: Old Town School describes itself as the largest nonprofit community arts school in the U.S.; MacArthur says it serves 6,000+ students per week and 16,500 registered students annually.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Class/event foot traffic; nonprofit payroll; arts education; restaurants/retail spillover; local identity
anchors.rationale: Old Town School is a smaller employer than Swedish but a powerful corridor amplifier: students, families, volunteers, concertgoers, and event attendees can drive repeat local spending on Lincoln Avenue.
anchors.validationNeeded: Estimate annual foot traffic by campus; measure spending spillover to restaurants, cafes, bookstores, and local retailers.

anchors.name: Lane Tech College Prep
anchors.site: 2501 W. Addison St., Chicago, IL 60618
anchors.evidenceScale: CPS says Lane Tech serves more than 4,500 students; Illinois Report Card confirms the 2501 W. Addison address.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Education workforce; student/family traffic; long-run human capital; public investment
anchors.rationale: Lane Tech is a civic and human-capital anchor. Its near-term neighborhood multiplier comes from staff, families, students, events, and local vendors; its long-term impact comes from education and workforce preparation.
anchors.validationNeeded: Estimate staff count, local procurement, and event attendance; separate neighborhood spillover from citywide student draw.

anchors.name: WGN-TV Studios
anchors.site: 2501 W. Bradley Place, Chicago, IL 60618
anchors.evidenceScale: Hines reports the WGN-TV Studios building is 131,000 square feet and fully leased to WGN-TV in Chicago's North Center submarket.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Media payroll; production services; contractors; professional services; local brand visibility
anchors.rationale: WGN is a real company-level anchor with a major physical campus. Its local multiplier is plausible but less visible than Lane Tech because employee count and local procurement are not publicly transparent.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm site-level employment and local vendor spend; identify production contractors, facilities vendors, and media talent pipelines.

anchors.name: Advocate Illinois Masonic Medical Center
anchors.site: 836 W. Wellington Ave., Chicago, IL 60657
anchors.evidenceScale: Advocate lists the Lake View address; official/clinical profiles describe Illinois Masonic as a comprehensive nonprofit medical center with Level I trauma and Level III NICU capabilities.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Hospital payroll; health-care jobs; patient/visitor traffic; medical procurement; community health access
anchors.rationale: Illinois Masonic is Lake View's most grounded employment and essential-service anchor. It combines stable health-care jobs with visitor traffic and strong demand for suppliers, facilities, food, professional services, and transportation.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm current employee count and local-resident hiring share; quantify neighborhood procurement and patient/visitor spending.

anchors.name: Chicago Cubs / Wrigley Field
anchors.site: 1060 W. Addison St., Chicago, IL 60613
anchors.evidenceScale: The Cubs cite nearly 7,000 jobs, $244M in personal annual earnings, $638M in annual economic activity, 80+ nearby businesses directly affected, and average fan spending of $104 per visit.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Visitor spending; hospitality jobs; bars/restaurants; transportation; event-driven retail; grants/community investments
anchors.rationale: Wrigley Field's strength is not just team payroll; it is the ability to import large volumes of fans and visitors into the neighborhood and push spending into bars, restaurants, rooftops, hotels, parking, and retail.
anchors.validationNeeded: Separate Cubs/Wrigley-specific impact from broader Lake View hospitality; estimate local vendor and local hiring shares.

anchors.name: DePaul University
anchors.site: Lincoln Park Campus, Chicago, IL
anchors.evidenceScale: DataUSA reports $278M in 2023 salary expenditures and 21,348 total students; recent reporting notes DePaul remains a Lincoln Park-based university despite 2025 staff reductions.
anchors.multiplierChannels: University payroll; student/family spending; procurement; real estate/capital projects; workforce development
anchors.rationale: DePaul is the strongest institutional employer and daily-population anchor in Lincoln Park. Its multiplier comes from payroll, student housing and spending, events, campus services, and vendor procurement.
anchors.validationNeeded: Split Lincoln Park campus employment/spend from university-wide totals; assess the effect of recent staff reductions on local spending.

anchors.name: Lincoln Park Zoo
anchors.site: 2400 N. Cannon Drive, Chicago, IL 60614
anchors.evidenceScale: Lincoln Park Zoo is free and open daily; annual reports describe more than 3M annual visitors and operating costs of nearly $39M per year, with visitors/donors funding more than 80% of the budget.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Tourism/visitor spending; nonprofit payroll; education/conservation; parking/food/retail spillover; free cultural access
anchors.rationale: The zoo is a high-foot-traffic anchor with a public-good multiplier: it draws residents and tourists into Lincoln Park while keeping admission free, supporting nearby restaurants, retail, parking, transit, and family-oriented visits.
anchors.validationNeeded: Estimate neighborhood capture of visitor spending and current staff count; distinguish zoo spillover from broader park/lakefront tourism.

anchors.name: Northwestern Memorial Hospital / Northwestern Medicine
anchors.site: Northwestern Memorial Hospital, 251 E. Huron St.; Streeterville medical campus
anchors.evidenceScale: Northwestern Medicine publicly describes itself as the 3rd largest private employer in Illinois. Northwestern Memorial Hospital is its downtown academic medical center, with nearly every medical specialty represented and a Feinberg School of Medicine partnership.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Large payroll; patient and visitor spending; medical procurement; workforce training; hotel/restaurant spillover; supplier and construction demand.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm site-specific employment and vendor spend within the Near North Side rather than systemwide Illinois figures.

anchors.name: Navy Pier
anchors.site: 600 E. Grand Ave.; lakefront tourism and cultural destination
anchors.evidenceScale: Navy Pier describes itself as the Midwest's most-visited destination, welcoming nearly nine million guests annually, with more than 800 employees and 70 on-site tenant partners.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Visitor spending; event vendor opportunities; tenant payroll; restaurants/retail/cruises; seasonal jobs; cultural programming.
anchors.validationNeeded: Estimate how much visitor spending is captured by Near North Side businesses vs. tenant/parking/event spend that leaks elsewhere.

anchors.name: Edison Park Chamber / Northwest Highway restaurant and business corridor
anchors.type: Local business corridor / independent business cluster
anchors.site: Commercial district around Northwest Highway, Olmsted/Ozark/Oshkosh, and Edison Park Metra
anchors.evidenceScale: The Edison Park Chamber says it has advocated for local businesses for more than 30 years and is located inside the Edison Park Metra Station. Edison Park Fest reports nearly 20,000 attendees and uses proceeds for beautification, community programs, and school/civic fundraisers.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Restaurant payroll; local vendor spend; visitor/event spending; chamber-led reinvestment; corridor beautification; commuter-adjacent foot traffic.
anchors.validationNeeded: Needs establishment-level employment, business count, and local ownership verification; this is a corridor cluster, not a single employer.

anchors.name: Edison Park civic education anchors: Edison Park Elementary + St. Juliana School/Parish
anchors.site: Edison Park Elementary, 6220 N. Olcott Ave.; St. Juliana School/Parish, Edison Park area
anchors.evidenceScale: CPS describes Edison Park Elementary as a neighborhood school preparing students for college and career. St. Juliana describes its school as a parish ministry serving preschool through eighth grade.
anchors.multiplierChannels: School/parish staff payroll; family foot traffic; aftercare and events; youth development; local fundraising; household retention through neighborhood education.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm staff counts, enrollment, parish/school operating spend, and whether other local businesses employ more people.

anchors.name: Prime Healthcare Resurrection Medical Center
anchors.site: 7435 W. Talcott Ave.
anchors.evidenceScale: Prime completed acquisition of multiple Ascension Illinois hospitals in 2025. Resurrection Medical Center is listed at 7435 W. Talcott Ave. and described as an academic teaching hospital with a Level II emergency department, birthing center, cancer and heart disease services, and stroke/chest pain designations.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Hospital payroll; clinical and support jobs; patient/visitor spending; medical supplies; facilities/maintenance; health-care retention on the far northwest side.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm current site employment after Prime acquisition and local procurement/community-benefit commitments.

anchors.name: Norwood Crossing / Norwood Seniors Network
anchors.type: Nonprofit senior living / skilled nursing / rehab
anchors.site: 6016 N. Nina Ave.
anchors.evidenceScale: Norwood Crossing describes itself as a nonprofit senior living community in historic Norwood Park offering assisted living, memory support, skilled nursing, rehabilitation, and respite care. Its history page says it serves more than 250 residents.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Health-care and care-worker payroll; service-gap closure for seniors; family visitor spending; local nonprofit reinvestment; rehab and nursing supply demand.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm employee count and annual operating budget; Taft High School is a close civic alternate if student scale is weighted more heavily.

anchors.name: Copernicus Center / Gateway Theater
anchors.type: Cultural venue / event center / nonprofit foundation
anchors.site: 5216 W. Lawrence Ave.; adjacent to Jefferson Park transit hub
anchors.evidenceScale: The Copernicus Center describes itself as a premier event center hosting concerts, theatre, workshops, cultural activities, community engagement, and Taste of Polonia. Gateway Theater states it seats up to 1,800.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Event-driven visitor spending; food/vendor opportunities; cultural tourism; venue employment and contractors; neighborhood visibility; nonprofit reinvestment.
anchors.validationNeeded: Quantify annual attendance, vendor spend, staffing, and business spillover on Lawrence/Milwaukee.

anchors.name: Jefferson Park Transit Center
anchors.site: 4917 N. Milwaukee Ave.; CTA Blue Line, CTA buses, Pace, Metra UP-NW
anchors.evidenceScale: CTA identifies Jefferson Park as an accessible Blue Line station with connections to multiple CTA bus lines, Pace routes, Pulse Milwaukee Line, and Metra UP-NW.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Commuter foot traffic; transit-oriented development; corridor visibility; customer access for local businesses; lower transportation friction for workers.
anchors.validationNeeded: Transit is an enabling anchor, not an employer; pair with business license/LODES data to see which nearby firms capture spending.

anchors.name: Edgebrook-Sauganash Chamber / North Branch Market local business ecosystem
anchors.site: Edgebrook, Sauganash, Devon/Central/Peterson/Cicero business nodes
anchors.evidenceScale: The Edgebrook-Sauganash Chamber says its mission is to serve, foster growth, and advocate for businesses in Edgebrook and Sauganash, and it supports the North Branch Market team.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Independent business retention; local vendors; chamber events; merchant collaboration; corridor foot traffic; neighborhood identity.
anchors.validationNeeded: Needs business count, member list, and establishment employment; Forest Glen lacks an obvious large single-employer anchor.

anchors.name: Whole Foods Market Sauganash
anchors.site: 6020 N. Cicero Ave.
anchors.evidenceScale: Whole Foods lists its Sauganash store at 6020 N. Cicero Ave. with grocery delivery/pickup, catering, store amenities, events, and careers.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Grocery-spending retention; store jobs; catering and prepared-food demand; everyday foot traffic; reduced leakage to suburban grocers.
anchors.validationNeeded: Chain ownership lowers local recirculation; validate employee count and any local supplier/community giving relationships.

anchors.name: Northeastern Illinois University
anchors.type: Public university / workforce and education anchor
anchors.site: Main Campus, 5500 N. St. Louis Ave.; 67-acre campus
anchors.evidenceScale: NEIU reports 5,756 total students, a 67-acre main campus on the Northwest Side, and a diverse student body. The main campus address is 5500 N. St. Louis Ave.
anchors.multiplierChannels: University payroll; student spending; public-sector jobs; procurement; workforce credentials; community partnerships; campus events.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm employee count, local procurement, student residential/spending patterns, and partnership spending in North Park.

anchors.name: North Park University
anchors.site: 3225 W. Foster Ave.; 30-acre campus
anchors.evidenceScale: North Park University reports 2,631 students enrolled, a 15:1 student-faculty ratio, and 30 acres in Chicago; its campus is at 3225 W. Foster Ave.
anchors.multiplierChannels: University payroll; student and visitor spending; procurement; nonprofit/community mission; internships and career training; campus events.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm employee count, student commuting patterns, local vendor use, and neighborhood business capture around Foster/Kedzie.

anchors.name: Albany Park Chamber / North River Commission / SSA #60 business districts
anchors.type: Economic development nonprofit + immigrant business corridor cluster
anchors.site: Lawrence, Kedzie, Kimball, Montrose, and Irving Park SSA corridors
anchors.evidenceScale: North River Commission describes itself as a community-based economic development nonprofit serving the northwest side and as a delegate agency/NBDC building thriving business districts with the Albany Park Chamber and SSA #60. The Chamber describes Albany Park as a highly diverse business community where over 40 languages are spoken in local schools.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Local business assistance; immigrant entrepreneurship; restaurant and retail payroll; facade/outdoor dining investments; local procurement; corridor foot traffic.
anchors.validationNeeded: Translate corridor ecosystem into business counts, jobs, sales-tax signal, and local ownership; this is a cluster, not one company.

anchors.name: Carole Robertson Center for Learning at Albany Park / former Albany Park Community Center
anchors.type: Social services / early childhood / workforce and family support
anchors.site: 5101 N. Kimball Ave.
anchors.evidenceScale: The former Albany Park Community Center is described as the largest social service agency exclusively serving Albany Park, with a wide range of programs and services; Carole Robertson Center took over the center in 2021 to expand early childhood education and family support.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Social-service jobs; childcare and early learning; workforce and adult education; food/security support; service-gap closure; family economic mobility.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm current post-merger employee count and program budget at the Albany Park site; Roosevelt and Haugan schools are major additional education anchors.

anchors.name: Community First Medical Center
anchors.multiplierChannels: Payroll; healthcare service retention; procurement; patient/visitor traffic
anchors.rationale: Community First is a site-specific hospital anchor at 5645 W. Addison. The Hospital Report Card confirms the Portage Park/Northwest Side hospital address and state designations, while public employer profiles indicate a large hospital workforce. It anchors local healthcare access, creates stable payroll, and can support nearby food, pharmacy, transportation, facilities, and professional-service demand.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm current FTE count, worker residency, local procurement categories, patient origin, and major capital projects.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Hospital benefits may spill across multiple Northwest Side neighborhoods, not only Portage Park.

anchors.name: Six Corners commercial and redevelopment district
anchors.multiplierChannels: Vacant property activation; retail and restaurant foot traffic; local small-business ecosystem
anchors.rationale: Six Corners is the strongest neighborhood commercial anchor because its multiplier comes from activating vacant and underused properties, adding housing and retail, and increasing foot traffic around a historic shopping district. Its impact is less about one employer and more about the density of businesses, tenants, restaurants, events, and redevelopment sites.
anchors.validationNeeded: Track actual tenant openings, vacancies, local ownership share, construction spend, and foot traffic before and after major projects.
anchors.leakageCaveat: District spans multiple corridors and will affect adjacent community areas as well.

anchors.name: Irving Park Blue Line / Metra / SSA #60 transit-business node
anchors.multiplierChannels: Transit foot traffic; small-business advising; corridor retention; visitor/customer access
anchors.rationale: The strongest multiplier candidate is the Irving Park transit and business-support node, combining Blue Line, Metra, bus connections, and North River Commission/SSA #60 business district support. This is a corridor multiplier: it can convert commuter flows into local spending and help independent businesses capture nearby demand.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate pedestrian counts, commercial vacancy, business mix, and local merchant sales before/after corridor interventions.
anchors.leakageCaveat: The node draws from Irving Park, Albany Park, Old Irving Park, and adjacent neighborhoods.

anchors.name: Cermak Fresh Market - Irving Park / Kedzie
anchors.multiplierChannels: Daily-needs spending; grocery/service-gap retention; jobs; repeat foot traffic
anchors.rationale: Cermak Fresh Market at Irving Park/Kedzie is a practical everyday-spending anchor. Grocery anchors can reduce leakage by keeping routine household spending in the neighborhood and by creating reliable local trips that benefit adjacent stores and restaurants.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm site employment, local vendor use, shoppershed, and whether anchor spending spills to nearby independent merchants.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Grocery catchment may include Albany Park and North Park households as well as Irving Park.

anchors.name: Wilbur Wright College
anchors.multiplierChannels: Workforce development; student spending; adult education; employer partnerships
anchors.rationale: Wright College is the clearest Dunning anchor because its main campus is at 4300 N. Narragansett and City Colleges describes it as a workforce-oriented campus with engineering/computer-science emphasis, career programs, adult education, and student-support services. The multiplier is strongest through local human-capital formation and nearby student/staff spending.
anchors.validationNeeded: Quantify student/staff counts by campus, local enrollment, graduate placement, and vendor contracts.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Students and employees may commute from across the Northwest Side, so neighborhood retention needs measurement.

anchors.name: Chicago-Read Mental Health Center
anchors.multiplierChannels: Public-sector jobs; healthcare service retention; specialized behavioral health; supplier demand
anchors.rationale: Chicago-Read is a major public health/care anchor in Dunning. Its multiplier is grounded in specialized behavioral healthcare, public-sector employment, and ongoing operating needs, though the publicly available data is less transparent than for a college or hospital.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current employment, bed count, services, procurement, and community-area boundary fit.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Institutional campus benefits may be less visible to adjacent small businesses than retail or education anchors.

anchors.name: Mont Clare Metra station / Grand Avenue transit-retail node
anchors.multiplierChannels: Commuter access; corridor foot traffic; small retail; leakage reduction
anchors.rationale: Montclare lacks a dominant site-specific private employer. The most realistic multiplier anchor is the Mont Clare station and adjacent Grand Avenue commercial node. The opportunity is to intercept commuter and household spending that otherwise leaks to Elmwood Park, Galewood, or regional centers.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate boardings, pedestrian counts, business inventory, vacancy, and resident shopping leakage.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Small geography and adjacency to suburbs mean economic benefits may cross city/suburb boundaries quickly.

anchors.name: Harlem / Grand commercial corridor + Sayre civic-service cluster
anchors.multiplierChannels: Family-serving civic activity; neighborhood retail; local services; corridor retention
anchors.rationale: The second anchor is a civic/commercial cluster rather than a single employer: Harlem/Grand Avenue businesses, Sayre Language Academy, and nearby library/family-serving services. This is a low-density retention play focused on keeping household spending and services in the neighborhood.
anchors.validationNeeded: Use business license and LODES data to identify larger employers; validate school enrollment/staff and corridor merchant counts.
anchors.leakageCaveat: This anchor is weaker and should be revisited if employer-level data identifies a stronger establishment.

anchors.name: Northwest Center + Belmont Cragin corridor system
anchors.multiplierChannels: Small-business technical assistance; local entrepreneurship; corridor investments; resident wealth-building
anchors.rationale: Northwest Center/Northwest Side CDC is a stronger local-retention anchor than many single businesses because it deliberately supports Belmont Cragin corridors, entrepreneurs, residents, and place-based investment. This anchor connects capital to local ownership and corridor health.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate business outcomes: jobs retained/created, sales growth, capital deployed, and corridor vacancy change.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Community development impacts take time and should be measured through program outcomes, not just footprint.

anchors.name: The Brickyard / Bricktown Square retail cluster
anchors.multiplierChannels: Retail jobs; grocery and household spending capture; regional customer draw
anchors.rationale: The Brickyard/Bricktown retail cluster is a large daily-needs and regional-shopping anchor for Belmont Cragin. Its strength is household-spending capture and employment, while its weakness is leakage through national-chain ownership and supply chains.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm current tenant employment, vacancies, customer origin, and share of sales captured by local residents.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Chain retail creates direct and induced impacts but weaker local ownership/profit retention.

anchors.name: Pulaski Industrial Corridor / Hermosa light-industrial employment base
anchors.type: Industrial corridor / production and logistics ecosystem
anchors.multiplierChannels: Local jobs; B2B spend; industrial property activation; vendor loops
anchors.rationale: Hermosa’s strongest multiplier potential is likely in the Pulaski industrial/commercial corridor, where older industrial and commercial properties can support production, logistics, repair, trades, food businesses, and B2B services. The opportunity is to identify specific employers and connect them to local hiring and vendor pipelines.
anchors.validationNeeded: Identify and verify specific top employers with LODES, business licenses, and field validation.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Corridor extends through multiple community areas and requires parcel-level boundary checks.

anchors.name: Kelvyn Park Junior & Senior High School
anchors.multiplierChannels: Student/family activity; workforce pathways; civic activity; neighborhood identity
anchors.rationale: Kelvyn Park is a civic and youth-workforce anchor in Hermosa. It matters economically because schools shape long-term human capital and can host allied health, digital media, arts, JROTC, family engagement, and school-to-career partnerships.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate enrollment, staff count, pathway employer partners, and neighborhood student share.
anchors.leakageCaveat: School-based multiplier is long-term and indirect compared with hospitals or large employers.

anchors.name: Revolution Brewing production brewery and taproom
anchors.multiplierChannels: Manufacturing jobs; local vendor supply; visitor spending; brand draw
anchors.rationale: Revolution Brewing’s Avondale production brewery/taproom is a strong company-level anchor. It combines production jobs, hospitality, visitor spending, and local supplier demand in a sector with potential for neighborhood-recursive spending.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm current site employment, supplier geography, visitor spend, and manufacturing procurement categories.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Impacts may extend into Logan Square and Irving Park due to customer geography and brand draw.

anchors.name: The Fields / Diversey-Pulaski adaptive reuse cluster
anchors.multiplierChannels: Vacant property activation; grocery/service retention; retail jobs; maker/industrial space
anchors.rationale: The Fields is a major adaptive-reuse and service-retail anchor around the former Marshall Field’s warehouse. It is important because it turns large industrial real estate into a grocery, retail, office/maker, industrial, and residential ecosystem that can capture local spending and support jobs.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current occupancy, employment, local hiring, and whether benefits are counted to Avondale versus Logan Square/Hermosa.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Boundary and brand geography are fuzzy; allocate impact carefully across adjacent community areas.

anchors.name: Milwaukee Avenue / Logan Square Chamber independent business corridor
anchors.type: Independent commercial corridor / entertainment and restaurant district
anchors.multiplierChannels: Independent business recirculation; restaurant/nightlife foot traffic; local vendor networks; cultural events
anchors.rationale: Logan Square’s highest multiplier is corridor-based. The Milwaukee Avenue and chamber/SSA ecosystem links independent restaurants, bars, retailers, arts/culture, and neighborhood-serving businesses. This anchor is especially strong for induced spending and local ownership recirculation.
anchors.validationNeeded: Measure merchant ownership, worker residency, rent pressure, local vendor use, and visitor/customer spending.
anchors.leakageCaveat: High market demand can create displacement; multiplier strategy should include retention and equity protections.

anchors.name: The Fields / 4000 W. Diversey mixed-use cluster
anchors.multiplierChannels: Grocery-service retention; adaptive reuse; jobs; local trips; tenant ecosystem
anchors.rationale: The Fields is also a major anchor for Logan Square due to its scale, service-retail draw, and adaptive reuse of an industrial property. Its multiplier is strongest through grocery spending capture, jobs, and property activation.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current tenant mix, employment, local ownership, and which side of the community-area boundary captures the effects.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Impacts overlap with Avondale/Hermosa; assign carefully in final modeling.

anchors.name: Humboldt Park Health / Wellness Center
anchors.multiplierChannels: Healthcare jobs; service-gap closure; patient and visitor traffic; community wellness
anchors.rationale: Humboldt Park Health is the most grounded institutional anchor: the hospital is located at 1044 N. Francisco and operates 24/7. Its own site frames the Wellness Center as an anchor institution that can transform neighborhood health and well-being. This is a high service-retention and payroll multiplier.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm current FTE, vendor geography, patient origin, and Wellness Center economic programming.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Hospital serves a broader West/Northwest Side population, so neighborhood-retained impact needs local data.

anchors.name: Paseo Boricua / Division Street cultural-business corridor
anchors.type: Cultural commercial corridor / legacy business ecosystem
anchors.multiplierChannels: Legacy business retention; cultural tourism; arts/economic anchor; local ownership
anchors.rationale: Paseo Boricua is a unique cultural and commercial anchor. WTTW describes Division Street/Paseo Boricua as the heart of Chicago’s Puerto Rican community and highlights cultural development intended to stimulate longtime businesses and create new ones. This makes it a strong retention, identity, and foot-traffic multiplier.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate merchant counts, cultural event attendance, local ownership, and business revenue trends.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Benefits are vulnerable to displacement pressures and require equity-centered retention metrics.

anchors.name: Saint Mary of Nazareth Hospital / Prime Healthcare St. Mary’s
anchors.multiplierChannels: Healthcare payroll; service retention; patient/visitor demand; procurement
anchors.rationale: Saint Mary of Nazareth is the strongest site-based institutional anchor in West Town, located on W. Division. Hospital activity supports payroll, health-service retention, professional services, facilities contracts, and nearby patient/visitor spending.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm post-acquisition FTE, bed count, service lines, procurement, and community benefit commitments.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Hospital market area extends beyond West Town; local retention must be estimated.

anchors.name: Wicker Park-Bucktown / Milwaukee-Damen-North commercial district
anchors.multiplierChannels: Retail/restaurant foot traffic; visitor spending; independent business; corridor services
anchors.rationale: The Wicker Park-Bucktown SSA #33 and surrounding commercial district provide a major neighborhood and regional visitor-spending anchor. This anchor is important because dense restaurant, retail, nightlife, and service clusters can recirculate wages and support neighboring merchants.
anchors.validationNeeded: Measure local ownership share, sales leakage, chain saturation, worker residency, and displacement risk.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Wicker Park-Bucktown spans multiple community-area identities and may overlap with Logan Square/Bucktown perception.

anchors.name: The Loretto Hospital
anchors.multiplierChannels: Payroll; healthcare service retention; community programs; local hiring potential
anchors.rationale: Loretto is the clearest Austin anchor. Its careers page identifies it as the largest non-governmental employer in Austin and describes a community-based hospital role. The multiplier is grounded in stable jobs, healthcare access, and potential procurement and workforce pathways.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current FTE, worker residency, procurement geography, and community benefit outcomes.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Hospital draws from Austin and broader West Side; count only retained local impact in final modeling.

anchors.name: Former Mars Wrigley Galewood factory redevelopment / 2019 N. Oak Park Ave.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Vacant industrial activation; future jobs; community benefits; site redevelopment
anchors.rationale: This is not a current operating employer anchor and should not be treated like one. Its importance is redevelopment potential: the former Mars Wrigley Galewood factory site is a major industrial-property activation opportunity where community benefits, local hiring, and service-gap uses could shape future multiplier value.
anchors.validationNeeded: Track final redevelopment plan, developer commitments, jobs, local hiring, procurement, and community-service uses.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Current economic impact is lower because the factory closed; score reflects potential and site scale, not current payroll.

anchors.name: Sankofa Wellness Village
anchors.type: Community health and economic development campus
anchors.multiplierChannels: Health services; jobs; community ownership; financial inclusion; entrepreneurship
anchors.rationale: Sankofa Wellness Village is the strongest West Garfield Park anchor because it combines healthcare, wellness, workforce, entrepreneurship, a community grocer, credit union/cafe, and community reinvestment. Public funder descriptions frame it as a transformative health and economic development project.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate opening timeline, tenant mix, operating budgets, job creation, procurement, and resident ownership/reinvestment mechanisms.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Some benefits are prospective until facilities are fully open and operating.

anchors.name: Madison-Pulaski corridor / Garfield Park Rite to Wellness ecosystem
anchors.multiplierChannels: Corridor revitalization; local businesses; food access; financial services; resident ownership
anchors.rationale: The second anchor is the Madison-Pulaski corridor ecosystem around Garfield Park Rite to Wellness. Its value comes from clustering services, local businesses, food access, and financial inclusion around a historically disinvested commercial node.
anchors.validationNeeded: Measure merchant count, sales, occupancy, local ownership, and corridor foot traffic.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Closely linked to Sankofa; avoid double-counting in final impact modeling.

anchors.name: The Hatchery Chicago
anchors.type: Food and beverage incubator / entrepreneurship anchor
anchors.multiplierChannels: Food entrepreneurship; shared production; jobs; training; local procurement
anchors.rationale: The Hatchery is the top East Garfield Park anchor. It is a nonprofit food and beverage incubator with shared kitchens, business support, training, financing connections, and a mission around local jobs and growth. IFF’s profile emphasizes the 67,000-square-foot facility, food-grade kitchens, startups, and job creation potential.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate active tenant count, jobs created, business survival, neighborhood resident participation, and procurement geography.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Incubator impacts can spread citywide; neighborhood retention depends on resident and vendor participation.

anchors.name: Garfield Park Conservatory / Green Line cultural-tourism anchor
anchors.multiplierChannels: Visitor draw; events; horticulture/culture jobs; adjacent corridor spending
anchors.rationale: The Garfield Park Conservatory is a major cultural and visitor anchor. It draws visitors, families, students, events, and programming into East Garfield Park and can create spillover demand for nearby food, retail, transit, and community businesses.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm attendance, event volume, visitor spending, local vendor/concession participation, and safety/wayfinding barriers.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Spillover is not automatic; corridor connection and visitor conversion must be designed.

anchors.name: Illinois Medical District / Rush-UIC-Cook County-Jesse Brown cluster
anchors.type: Healthcare, education, research, and life-sciences district
anchors.multiplierChannels: Massive employment; procurement; clinical services; research; workforce pathways
anchors.rationale: The Illinois Medical District is the strongest anchor in this combined batch. It is a concentrated healthcare, education, research, and technology district on the Near West Side. Its local multiplier depends on how well hiring, procurement, and spinout activity connect to surrounding West Side residents and vendors.
anchors.validationNeeded: Quantify site employment by institution, local/resident hires, procurement by ZIP/community area, and patient/visitor spending.
anchors.leakageCaveat: District-level impacts are huge but may leak outside the Near West Side without intentional local capture.

anchors.name: United Center / The 1901 Project
anchors.multiplierChannels: Event-day visitor spending; construction jobs; permanent jobs; hotels/retail; West Side redevelopment
anchors.rationale: The United Center is already a major sports and entertainment draw, and the proposed 1901 Project adds a large redevelopment engine. Public materials describe a major private investment and projected construction/permanent jobs. The caution is that future-project impacts should be separated from current event-day impact.
anchors.validationNeeded: Separate current United Center operations from projected 1901 impacts; verify approvals, timeline, local hiring, procurement, and spillover capture.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Projected impacts are not realized impacts. Treat them as scenario/pipeline value until delivered.

anchors.name: Mount Sinai Hospital / Sinai Chicago
anchors.site: 1500 S. Fairfield Ave. / Ogden Commons area, North Lawndale
anchors.evidenceScale: City of Chicago described Mount Sinai as North Lawndale's largest employer with 4,100 full- and part-time employees; Sinai also operates community health and social-service programs.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Direct payroll; healthcare access; local hiring pipelines; vendor/contractor procurement; patient/family foot traffic; nonprofit/community benefit.
anchors.rationale: The anchor combines large-site payroll, patient traffic, healthcare service retention, and potential procurement through campus operations, construction, food, facilities, and community programming.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm current FTE/headcount, resident-worker share, procurement share to North Lawndale/West Side vendors, and current Ogden Commons utilization.
anchors.leakageCaveat: The clearest public site-employment figure is dated; current site headcount should be validated directly with Sinai.

anchors.name: Lawndale Christian Health Center
anchors.site: 3860 W. Ogden Ave. and related Lawndale sites
anchors.evidenceScale: Annual/leadership materials report roughly 625-637 staff in recent years and describe a community-serving health center with a local hiring emphasis and tens of thousands of patients.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Primary care; dental/behavioral health; local hiring; workforce exposure; induced wage spending; neighborhood trust and retention.
anchors.rationale: Smaller than Sinai but deeply embedded: it closes primary-care access gaps, hires locally, trains workers, anchors daily patient traffic, and reinvests through community-based health and social services.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm 2025/2026 employee count, patient count, percent staff living in North/South Lawndale, and local purchasing practices.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Current staff, patient, and local-resident hiring numbers should be refreshed from the latest annual report or direct interview.

anchors.name: 26th Street / Little Village Commercial Corridor
anchors.site: 26th Street corridor, Little Village
anchors.evidenceScale: Foundation of Little Village describes the two-mile 26th Street corridor as the backbone of the local economy with over 500 small businesses; media and corridor plans identify it as one of Chicago's busiest retail districts.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Foot traffic; small-business revenue retention; local hiring; local vendor networks; cultural tourism; corridor improvements.
anchors.rationale: This is a cluster anchor rather than one employer: dense locally rooted storefronts capture household spending, visitor spending, food purchases, services, and small-business B2B activity.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate active storefront count, sales tax by corridor, vacancy rate, local ownership share, and local employment estimates.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Sales figures cited publicly are older; update with current sales tax, business-license, vacancy, and foot-traffic data.

anchors.name: Saint Anthony Hospital / Focal Point Community Campus
anchors.site: Current Saint Anthony Hospital at 2875 W. 19th St.; proposed Focal Point campus at 31st/Kedzie
anchors.evidenceScale: Focal Point is planned as a mixed-use campus anchored by Saint Anthony Hospital on 30 contiguous acres, serving an area of more than 440,000 people.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Healthcare access; direct hospital jobs; construction jobs; patient/visitor traffic; retail/service co-location; redevelopment of underutilized land.
anchors.rationale: The hospital anchors service-gap closure and payroll now; Focal Point adds potential construction, healthcare, retail, wellness, education, and recreation spillovers if delivered with local hiring and procurement.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm project delivery status, current hospital headcount, procurement policy, and local hiring commitments.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Part of the multiplier is pipeline-dependent; do not count projected Focal Point jobs until financing, construction, tenanting, and community-benefit terms are validated.

anchors.name: Alivio Medical Center
anchors.site: Pilsen health centers, school-based clinics, and related Near Southwest Side locations
anchors.evidenceScale: Alivio describes comprehensive community healthcare with an emphasis on maternal and child health; provider profiles note multiple Pilsen locations plus South Lawndale school-based health centers.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Healthcare access; local hiring; patient traffic; bilingual service retention; social-service referrals; induced payroll spending.
anchors.rationale: Alivio anchors bilingual/bicultural care, reduces health-service leakage, brings daily patient visits, and supports jobs connected to healthcare, outreach, and administrative operations.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm current headcount, patient volume, payer mix, service lines, and neighborhood residency of staff.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Employee count and current financial stability should be validated due recent sector funding pressures.

anchors.name: National Museum of Mexican Art / 18th Street Cultural Corridor
anchors.site: 1852 W. 19th St. and Pilsen/18th Street corridor
anchors.evidenceScale: The museum reports/partners describe more than 150,000 annual visitors and tens of thousands of K-12 students served; 18th Street is the heart of Pilsen's commercial and cultural activity.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Visitor spending; education visits; restaurant/retail spillover; local artists; event rentals; cultural identity retention.
anchors.rationale: Cultural visitors, students, families, events, galleries, restaurants, and nearby shops create a high foot-traffic multiplier for independent businesses and culturally rooted entrepreneurship.
anchors.validationNeeded: Estimate museum visitors' Pilsen spending, corridor business count, vacancy rate, and local artist/vendor participation.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Visitor spending retained inside Pilsen is not published; needs survey or corridor sales analysis.

anchors.name: Art Institute of Chicago / Millennium Park / Loop Arts District
anchors.site: Michigan Avenue/Monroe area, Millennium Park, State Street arts district
anchors.evidenceScale: Millennium Park is cited as drawing very large annual visitation and driving tourism/business; the Chicago Loop Alliance has reported major arts/culture attendance and economic impact in the Loop.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Tourism; visitor food/retail/hotel spend; cultural jobs; event production; vendors; downtown placemaking.
anchors.rationale: This cluster imports external dollars through visitors, events, restaurants, hotels, retail, rideshare/transit, and cultural programming; it is the Loop's strongest foot-traffic-based multiplier.
anchors.validationNeeded: Update with latest visitor counts, event attendance, Loop Arts District membership, and spending per visitor.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Leakage is high because many vendors, owners, and workers are not Loop residents; use as district impact, not resident-only impact.

anchors.name: Willis Tower / Central Office-Employment Cluster
anchors.site: 233 S. Wacker Dr. and surrounding central business district
anchors.evidenceScale: Willis Tower is a major office/visitor asset; the Loop remains a global business district with Chicago Loop Alliance representing over 300 business, civic, and cultural institutions.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Office payroll; building services; professional services; commuter spending; retail/lunch demand; tourism.
anchors.rationale: Large office tenancy supports direct jobs, cleaning/security/facilities contracts, lunch/retail demand, event space, tourism through Skydeck, and broader downtown professional services.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm occupied SF, tenant headcount, Skydeck visitation, vendor spending, and worker foot-traffic recovery.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Neighborhood retention is limited because many workers commute and many firms procure through national or regional supply chains.

anchors.name: McCormick Place / Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority
anchors.site: 2301 S. King Dr. and surrounding convention campus
anchors.evidenceScale: McCormick Place describes itself as North America's largest convention center with more than 2.6 million square feet of exhibit space and roughly $2B+ annual economic impact.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Visitor spending; hospitality employment; event production; contractors; logistics; restaurant/retail spillover.
anchors.rationale: Convention visitors import spending into hotels, restaurants, transportation, event labor, construction/booth services, catering, cleaning, security, logistics, and nearby retail.
anchors.validationNeeded: Estimate neighborhood share of vendor contracts, local hotel/restaurant capture, and resident hiring from convention operations.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Impact is citywide/regional; neighborhood retention depends on South Loop vendor participation and local hiring.

anchors.name: Museum Campus / Soldier Field Event District
anchors.type: Museums, stadium, parks, and event assets
anchors.site: Museum Campus, Soldier Field, lakefront South Loop
anchors.evidenceScale: Museum Campus includes major attractions such as Shedd Aquarium, Field Museum, and Adler Planetarium; Soldier Field supports event/concession employment and visitor spending.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Visitor foot traffic; hospitality and concessions jobs; retail/restaurant spillover; event production; transit and parking spend.
anchors.rationale: The cluster creates repeat event and visitor flows that support hospitality, restaurants, parking, transit, concessions, retail, and family tourism near the Near South Side.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm annual visitor/attendance by asset, supplier/local business capture, and game-day/event-day spending patterns.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Some spending is captured by institutional operators and regional vendors; local business capture should be measured.

anchors.name: Chinatown Business District / Chinatown Chamber / SSA #73
anchors.type: Ethnic commercial district + business improvement district
anchors.site: Cermak/Wentworth/Archer Chinatown district
anchors.evidenceScale: Chinatown Chamber's mission is to expand business opportunities and attract visitors/investors; SSA #73 supports the economic well-being and tourism appeal of Chinatown.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Visitor dining/retail; small-business ownership; local hiring; corridor marketing; business support; cultural tourism.
anchors.rationale: Chinatown is a dense small-business and restaurant ecosystem with strong cultural tourism, independent business ownership, local services, and corridor-level reinvestment.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm active business count, tourism metrics, local hiring, vendor sourcing, and post-pandemic recovery trend.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Need business count, vacancy, sales tax, local ownership, and local-worker data to quantify retention.

anchors.name: Rate Field / Chicago White Sox
anchors.site: 333 W. 35th St., Armour Square/Bridgeport edge
anchors.evidenceScale: ISFA identifies the ballpark as the White Sox home stadium with public transit access and a capacity around 42,000; Baseball-Reference reports 2025 White Sox home attendance above 1.4M.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Event-day foot traffic; concessions; parking/transit; hospitality; security/cleaning jobs; sports tourism.
anchors.rationale: Game-day and event-day visitors can support concessions, bars/restaurants, parking, transit, security, cleaning, and seasonal jobs, especially if spending is captured by nearby businesses.
anchors.validationNeeded: Estimate spending captured by Armour Square/Chinatown businesses, seasonal jobs, vendor localization, and future lease/stadium uncertainty.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Sports-stadium multipliers are often overstated; much revenue leaks to team/stadium operators, and activity is episodic.

anchors.name: Illinois Institute of Technology
anchors.site: Mies Campus, Bronzeville/Douglas
anchors.evidenceScale: Illinois Tech is a major Bronzeville institution with roughly 6,500 students and a workforce including professional staff and full-time faculty; it also operates community-affairs programming.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Payroll; student spending; local procurement; STEM training; small-business support; events/facilities.
anchors.rationale: The campus supports student and employee spending, STEM workforce pipelines, procurement, event space, entrepreneurship programming, and neighborhood engagement through Bronzeville-oriented initiatives.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm current employee/student counts, South Side vendor spending, campus capital projects, and local resident participation.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Need procurement spend and local hiring data specific to Douglas/Bronzeville.

anchors.name: Insight Hospital and Medical Center Chicago
anchors.site: 2525 S. Michigan Ave., Bronzeville/Douglas
anchors.evidenceScale: Insight Chicago describes itself as a nonprofit safety-net hospital committed to Bronzeville; the former Mercy Hospital facility is a 414-bed hospital.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Direct healthcare jobs; patient access; visitor foot traffic; procurement; community health benefit; induced payroll spending.
anchors.rationale: The hospital anchors jobs, emergency and specialty care, patient/visitor traffic, and medical procurement while preserving a historic South Side healthcare asset.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current beds in service, employees, service utilization, procurement policy, and community-benefit commitments.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Current headcount and service-line scale should be confirmed after ownership/operating changes.

anchors.name: Lake Meadows Shopping Center / Jewel-anchored retail node
anchors.site: 35th Street and King Drive, Oakland/Douglas edge
anchors.evidenceScale: NewMark Merrill describes Lake Meadows as a 179,106-square-foot grocery-anchored neighborhood center on 16 acres, anchored by Jewel-Osco, LA Fitness, CVS, Foot Locker, Citi Trends, and other merchants.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Grocery/service retention; retail jobs; customer foot traffic; small-tenant opportunity; property reinvestment; induced spending.
anchors.rationale: For a neighborhood with a limited commercial base, a grocery-anchored retail center captures routine spending, fills daily-service gaps, and draws customer traffic from surrounding Bronzeville/Oakland blocks.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm official community-area boundary, tenant roster, employee count, local small-business tenant share, and shopper origin.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Boundary is near the Oakland/Douglas edge; local ownership and worker-residency data are likely limited.

anchors.name: Chicago Military Academy at Bronzeville / Eighth Regiment Armory
anchors.type: Public high school + historic civic asset
anchors.site: 3519 S. Giles Ave., Bronzeville/Oakland area
anchors.evidenceScale: CPS describes Chicago Military Academy as an Early College STEM school preparing cadets for college and post-secondary success; its site is tied to the historic Eighth Regiment Armory.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Education payroll; student/family foot traffic; workforce pathway; civic/historic identity; events.
anchors.rationale: The school is not a large economic anchor, but it is one of Oakland's clearest site-based civic anchors, supporting staff payroll, student/family activity, and longer-run workforce development.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm enrollment, staff count, community-area boundary, procurement, and local partnership programming.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Low direct multiplier compared with hospitals, universities, or large retail; best considered a civic/workforce anchor.

anchors.name: Fuller Park Community Development Corp / Eden Place Nature Center and Farms
anchors.site: 4417 S. Stewart Ave. and Fuller Park urban-agriculture sites
anchors.evidenceScale: Eden Place is described as a Fuller Park Community Development Corporation program; WTTW quoted FPCD leadership saying they had trained more than 3,000 men and women from the Fuller Park area.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Workforce training; urban agriculture; land activation; food access; community events; environmental remediation.
anchors.rationale: This anchor activates land, improves food access, trains residents, creates environmental and public-health benefits, and keeps impact tied directly to Fuller Park residents.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm current training completions, employees, farm revenue, produce distribution, capital plans, and partners.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Direct payroll and revenue scale are smaller than a hospital or industrial employer; grant dependence should be assessed.

anchors.name: Norfolk Southern 47th Street Intermodal / Rail-Industrial Corridor
anchors.site: 47th Street rail/intermodal area, Fuller Park industrial edge
anchors.evidenceScale: Norfolk Southern references its Chicago 47th Street facility; Chicago rail planning materials describe rail access as a unique industrial-development opportunity for the city.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Industrial jobs; logistics services; facility maintenance; contractor procurement; freight-linked business attraction.
anchors.rationale: Rail and logistics assets can support industrial jobs, freight-serving businesses, truck/maintenance services, and property-tax/industrial activity, but retention depends heavily on local hiring and environmental/community benefits.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm terminal boundaries, company/facility headcount, vendor spend, local hiring, truck impacts, and mitigation/community-benefit agreements.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Potentially high leakage and environmental externalities; not automatically a community wealth anchor without local hiring and mitigation commitments.

anchors.name: Provident Hospital of Cook County
anchors.site: 500 E. 51st St., Grand Boulevard
anchors.evidenceScale: Cook County Health lists Provident Hospital at 500 E. 51st Street and emphasizes high-quality care close to home through hospitals and community clinics.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Healthcare payroll; service-gap closure; patient traffic; public-sector stability; procurement; community health.
anchors.rationale: Provident anchors neighborhood healthcare access, stable public-sector health jobs, patient/visitor flow, health-sector purchasing, and service retention in Bronzeville/Grand Boulevard.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm current headcount, patient volume, beds in service, procurement approach, and neighborhood-resident worker share.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Hospital employment and service-line data need current validation; public hospital procurement may not localize to Grand Boulevard.

anchors.name: Chicago Urban League / Bronzeville 47th Street Commercial-Workforce Corridor
anchors.site: 4510 S. Michigan Ave. and 43rd/47th/51st Bronzeville corridors
anchors.evidenceScale: Chicago Urban League runs employment, entrepreneurship, finance, housing, youth, and workforce programs; Bronzeville corridor planning focuses on 43rd, 47th, and 51st Streets.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Workforce placement; entrepreneurship; small-business support; corridor spending; civic convening; local hiring.
anchors.rationale: The League and corridor ecosystem support resident job placement, entrepreneurship, small-business activation, and corridor foot traffic in the heart of Bronzeville.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm program outcomes by ZIP/community area, businesses served, placements, corridor vacancy, and storefront sales.
anchors.leakageCaveat: The exact neighborhood-level conversion from program participation to Grand Boulevard jobs/business revenue needs direct data.

anchors.name: University of Chicago Local / Kenwood-Hyde Park Campus Interface
anchors.category: Anchor procurement, jobs, education, real estate
anchors.site: Kenwood/Hyde Park campus-adjacent area and South Side catchment
anchors.evidenceScale: UChicago Civic Engagement describes UChicago Local as leveraging the University's role as the largest private employer and purchaser on the South Side to create opportunities for local businesses and residents.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Payroll; local procurement; student spending; workforce development; business diversity; real-estate/corridor investment.
anchors.rationale: UChicago's procurement, hiring, student activity, real-estate presence, and community programs shape Kenwood's local economy, though impacts cross community-area boundaries.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm Kenwood-specific payroll, procurement, student/employee spending, and local business participation.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Cross-boundary anchor; need to isolate Kenwood-specific impact from Hyde Park and Washington Park effects.

anchors.name: Little Black Pearl Art & Design Center
anchors.category: Youth development, creative workforce, cultural enterprise
anchors.site: 1060 E. 47th St., Kenwood/Bronzeville
anchors.evidenceScale: MacArthur describes Little Black Pearl as a 40,000-square-foot cultural arts center with courses and production space for arts, culture, and entrepreneurship, also operating an art and design academy.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Creative workforce; youth education; events; local artists; entrepreneurship; corridor foot traffic.
anchors.rationale: It supports youth/adult creative learning, event space, entrepreneurship, and cultural production on 47th Street, creating a local-talent and corridor-activation multiplier.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm current headcount, student/participant count, events, revenue, and local business/artist partnerships.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Scale is smaller than university/health anchors; current employment and annual participant data should be updated.

anchors.name: UChicago Arts + Public Life / Arts Block
anchors.category: Creative economy, corridor activation, local entrepreneurship
anchors.site: 301 E. Garfield Blvd. and Garfield Boulevard Arts Block
anchors.evidenceScale: Arts + Public Life describes itself as a neighborhood platform for arts and culture in Washington Park; Arts Block materials focus on Garfield Boulevard as an economically strong cultural corridor.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Creative entrepreneurship; local artists; public programming; vacant-property activation; corridor foot traffic; youth arts education.
anchors.rationale: The Arts Block activates vacant/underused property, supports artists and creative entrepreneurs, brings foot traffic to Garfield Boulevard, and builds a place-based corridor identity.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm annual attendance, resident artists/entrepreneurs supported, vendor/local procurement, and corridor business spillovers.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Payroll scale is limited; corridor sales/foot traffic and artist income effects need measurement.

anchors.name: DuSable Black History Museum and Education Center
anchors.site: 740 E. 56th Pl., Washington Park
anchors.evidenceScale: DuSable describes itself as the nation's first independent Black history museum and a South Side cultural institution dedicated to Black history, culture, and education.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Visitor spending; cultural jobs; school visits; events; vendor needs; tourism identity.
anchors.rationale: DuSable is a destination anchor that brings visitors, school groups, events, tourism dollars, and cultural identity to Washington Park and adjacent South Side corridors.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm annual attendance, events, employees, vendor spending, and visitor spend captured locally.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Local-retention effect depends on adjacent retail/restaurant capture, which is limited and needs corridor strengthening.

anchors.name: University of Chicago / UChicago Medicine Anchor Complex
anchors.site: Hyde Park campus and South Side medical campus
anchors.evidenceScale: UChicago Local describes the University as the largest private employer and purchaser on the South Side; UChicago Medicine reported $715M in community benefit investment for fiscal 2024 and $1.1B for fiscal 2025.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Major payroll; local procurement; healthcare access; research; student spending; patient/visitor spending; workforce development.
anchors.rationale: This is among Chicago's most powerful neighborhood anchors: payroll, procurement, research, students, patients, visitors, housing demand, retail demand, and community-benefit programming all interact locally.
anchors.validationNeeded: Isolate Hyde Park-specific employee, procurement, patient, student, and visitor spending data.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Very high cross-boundary impact; avoid double-counting with Kenwood, Washington Park, and Woodlawn.

anchors.name: Griffin Museum of Science and Industry
anchors.site: 5700 S. DuSable Lake Shore Dr., Jackson Park/Hyde Park
anchors.evidenceScale: The museum describes itself as one of the largest science centers in the Western Hemisphere; visitor sources describe it as a major Chicago attraction in Hyde Park.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Tourism; education visits; events; parking/transit; nearby retail/restaurant spending; cultural jobs.
anchors.rationale: MSI brings regional and tourist visitors who can support restaurants, retail, parking, transit, hotels, education vendors, events, and family-oriented visitor spending.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm annual attendance, employees, vendor spend, and visitor spend captured by Hyde Park businesses.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Visitor dollars may leak to parking/on-site operators or downtown hotels; local capture should be studied.

anchors.name: Obama Presidential Center / Jackson Park
anchors.site: Jackson Park / Woodlawn-Hyde Park edge
anchors.evidenceScale: City and Obama Foundation materials estimate 700,000 annual visitors, long-term impact above $3B, and thousands of direct/indirect/induced jobs during construction and operations.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Construction jobs; permanent operations jobs; visitor spending; small-business opportunities; tourism; public realm/corridor activation.
anchors.rationale: The center can become Woodlawn's strongest imported-spending anchor through construction, permanent operations, visitor traffic, hospitality, retail, food, cultural programming, and public-realm investment.
anchors.validationNeeded: Track opening timeline, permanent jobs, local hiring/procurement commitments, visitor spending, and anti-displacement outcomes.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Pipeline/implementation risk remains; local wealth impact depends on resident hiring, local procurement, anti-displacement, and corridor capture.

anchors.name: Friend Health / Woodlawn Family Health & Wellness Center
anchors.site: 6250 S. Cottage Grove Ave., Woodlawn
anchors.evidenceScale: Friend Health lists a Cottage Grove location at 6250 S. Cottage Grove; project materials describe the Woodlawn center as providing integrated health and wellness services in an underutilized space.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Healthcare jobs; patient traffic; behavioral health; immediate/primary care; vacant-space activation; community wellness.
anchors.rationale: This is a current, site-based health anchor that closes service gaps, brings regular patient visits, supports healthcare jobs, and can connect residents to care and community resources.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm employee count, annual patient visits, payer mix, services, neighborhood workforce share, and vendor spend.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Need current employee count, patient volume, and local procurement data.

anchors.name: South Shore Hospital
anchors.site: 8012 S. Crandon Ave.; acute-care hospital serving South Shore and the Southeast Side
anchors.evidenceScale: 170-bed acute-care facility; public profile describes a stand-alone safety-net hospital with roughly 371 employees, and prior CHNA materials indicate 470+ employees including medical staff.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Payroll; healthcare service retention; clinical/vendor procurement; emergency and inpatient care; local workforce pathway
anchors.rationale: The strongest site-specific institutional anchor in South Shore. It keeps essential healthcare spending and jobs in the community and can create induced household spending if hiring and employee residency remain local.
anchors.validationNeeded: Verify 2026 employment count, patient volume, and local-residency share; distinguish hospital-wide spend from neighborhood-retained spend.

anchors.name: South Shore Cultural Center / Cultural Center Park
anchors.site: 7059 S. South Shore Dr.; cultural center, park, beach, golf course, nature sanctuary, and event space
anchors.evidenceScale: Chicago Park District lists the facility at 7059 S. South Shore Dr.; Choose Chicago describes the site as a 65-acre park with ballrooms, meeting space, golf, beach, and nature sanctuary.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Visitor spending; event/vendor procurement; cultural programming; local arts; lakefront tourism spillover
anchors.rationale: A distinctive cultural and visitor-facing asset. Its multiplier depends on whether visitors, events, and vendors connect to South Shore restaurants, retailers, artists, and service providers.
anchors.validationNeeded: Estimate annual visits/events, local vendor spend, and spillover to 71st Street/South Shore Drive merchants.

anchors.name: Capital One / Discover Chatham Customer Care Center + Shine Bright Community Center
anchors.type: Financial services / customer operations / community space
anchors.site: 8560 S. Cottage Grove Ave.; repurposed former big-box retail site
anchors.evidenceScale: Opened as Discover's Chatham Customer Care Center; public materials describe a 1,000-seat call center, 126,000-127,000 SF reuse, community center, and an employment goal of roughly 1,000 jobs. Current Capital One listings reference the Chatham Customer Care Center at the same address.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Large-scale payroll; local hiring; adaptive reuse; training/tuition benefits; community-center programming; local catering/vendor opportunity
anchors.rationale: The most grounded company-level anchor in Chatham because it converts a vacant retail box into scaled jobs with an explicit local-hiring narrative and community space.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm 2026 headcount after Capital One/Discover transition and document current local-hiring share and vendor spend.

anchors.name: Chatham Business Association / 79th-Cottage Grove business ecosystem
anchors.site: Chatham and surrounding South Side commercial corridors, including 79th Street and Cottage Grove
anchors.evidenceScale: CBA describes customized small-business services including economic development, strategic planning, technical training, access to capital, marketing, and certification support.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Local vendor capacity; business retention; access to capital; corridor foot traffic; service-gap closure through neighborhood retail
anchors.rationale: This is a cluster anchor rather than a single employer. It matters because Chatham's multiplier depends on how much payroll from large anchors is captured by locally owned restaurants, retailers, banks, and service firms.
anchors.validationNeeded: Map member businesses, employment, business density, vacancies, and sales leakage; test whether Chicago Urban League's new Empowerment Center should be added.

anchors.name: Chicago Vocational Career Academy
anchors.site: 2100 E. 87th St.; CPS high school with early-college STEM programming
anchors.evidenceScale: CPS describes CVCA as an Early College STEM School enabling students to earn a high school diploma and college credits; school materials list the 2100 E. 87th St. address.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Workforce pipeline; education service retention; student/family daily activity; public employment; future career pathways
anchors.rationale: The strongest current institutional anchor because it links neighborhood youth to STEM and career credentials. The multiplier is long-run workforce development more than immediate payroll.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate enrollment, staff count, career certifications, employer partnerships, and local internship/apprenticeship placements.

anchors.name: Avalon Regal Theater / 79th-Stony Island cultural redevelopment
anchors.site: 1641 E. 79th St.; landmark theater near Avalon Park/South Shore boundary
anchors.evidenceScale: City landmark record lists the New Regal Theater at 1641 E. 79th St.; theater materials state renovation is underway with a planned reopening by 2026.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Cultural tourism; event foot traffic; renovation/construction spend; local vendors; creative economy; corridor activation
anchors.rationale: Potentially high symbolic and visitor-spending multiplier, but it should be treated as a pipeline anchor until operating schedule, capital stack, jobs, and vendor model are verified.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm reopening date, seating capacity, programming calendar, operating jobs, neighborhood vendor requirements, and boundary attribution.

anchors.name: Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park / PsiQuantum at former U.S. Steel South Works
anchors.site: Former U.S. Steel South Works lakefront site; South Chicago
anchors.evidenceScale: Public reports describe the former South Works site as a large-scale quantum campus with PsiQuantum as anchor tenant and construction/groundbreaking activity in 2025.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Construction jobs; technology and skilled jobs; supplier ecosystem; infrastructure investment; long-vacant land activation; university/industry partnerships
anchors.rationale: The largest future-facing economic anchor in Batch 7. Its neighborhood multiplier could be transformational, but only if local hiring, procurement, housing, and anti-displacement commitments are real and measurable.
anchors.validationNeeded: Separate projected regional impact from neighborhood-retained impact; verify construction timeline, local procurement, environmental safeguards, and workforce pipelines.

anchors.name: Chicago Family Health Center - South Chicago Health Center
anchors.site: 9119 S. Exchange Ave.; South Chicago clinic
anchors.evidenceScale: CFHC lists South Chicago Health Center at 9119 S. Exchange Ave., with extended clinic hours and 24-hour on-call support; CFHC says it is a network of South Side health centers and has 200+ employees across the organization.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Primary care access; local health employment; patient traffic; service-gap closure; community health; induced spending
anchors.rationale: A practical, current local-impact anchor: not a mega-employer, but it plugs healthcare leakage and serves residents who might otherwise leave the community for routine care.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm site-level employment, patient count, insurance mix, and local residency of staff.

anchors.name: Stony Island Commercial / Burnside Industrial Corridors TIF
anchors.site: Stony Island commercial area and Burnside Industrial Corridor
anchors.evidenceScale: City of Chicago describes the roughly 611-acre TIF as a tool to revitalize adjacent economic centers with job-generating investments.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Industrial retention; job-generating investment; land activation; B2B services; small manufacturing/logistics support
anchors.rationale: Burnside has limited publicly visible site-specific employer data, so the most honest anchor is the industrial district itself. Its multiplier depends on retaining and attracting job-generating industrial users.
anchors.validationNeeded: Use business license, LODES, parcel, and employer verification to identify specific operating companies inside the corridor.

anchors.name: 91st Street/Chesterfield Metra node + 95th Street corridor spillover
anchors.site: 91st St. and Dauphin Ave.; proximity to 95th Street corridor and Chicago State area
anchors.evidenceScale: Metra lists 91st Street/Chesterfield at 91st St. and Dauphin Ave.; Chicago's 95th Street Corridor Plan seeks equitable TOD between Halsted and Cottage Grove, with spillover relevance to Burnside's southern edge.
