anchors.multiplierChannels: Transit access; TOD potential; household mobility; cross-boundary retail capture; nearby mixed-use redevelopment
anchors.rationale: A modest but real anchor for a small, rail-defined community. This should not be overstated: it is more a connectivity and future-development hypothesis than a major current employer.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate station ridership, walkability, safety, land availability, and whether future 95th Street activity benefits Burnside residents.

anchors.name: Advocate Trinity Hospital
anchors.site: 2320 E. 93rd St.; Advocate Southland Health Network
anchors.evidenceScale: Advocate lists Trinity Hospital at 2320 E. 93rd St.; public facility profiles list the hospital and health-system affiliation, with third-party profiles reporting large staffed-bed and employee ranges.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Hospital payroll; medical procurement; patient/visitor activity; service-gap closure; healthcare career ladder; outpatient referrals
anchors.rationale: The strongest site-specific economic and service anchor in Calumet Heights. Healthcare multipliers are labor-intensive and reduce leakage for essential care.
anchors.validationNeeded: Verify current staffed beds, site headcount, patient volume, vendor spend, and local hiring share.

anchors.name: Bronzeville Children's Museum
anchors.site: 9301 S. Stony Island Ave.; children's museum
anchors.evidenceScale: Museum materials list the 9301 S. Stony Island location and regular tour hours; Choose Chicago describes it as the first and only African American children's museum in the country.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Family visitor traffic; educational programming; cultural tourism; school trips; local food/retail spillover
anchors.rationale: Smaller direct payroll than a hospital, but a unique cultural asset with visitor and equity value. It can anchor school/family traffic and strengthen Calumet Heights' cultural identity.
anchors.validationNeeded: Estimate annual visits, school partnerships, event frequency, local spending capture, and staff size.

anchors.name: Chicago State University / 95th Street university village plan
anchors.site: 9501 S. King Dr.; 167-acre campus and 95th Street development area
anchors.evidenceScale: CSU describes itself as well positioned to anchor economic and real estate development along 95th Street, with 167 acres and open land; DataUSA reports 2,324 students in 2023.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Education/workforce pipeline; campus payroll; student spending; real estate development; university village retail; community programming
anchors.rationale: The strongest Roseland anchor because it combines operating jobs, student flow, land, and a corridor development strategy capable of filling service gaps and attracting complementary retail.
anchors.validationNeeded: Verify staff count, student residency, procurement policy, development schedule, and community-benefit commitments.

anchors.name: Roseland Community Hospital
anchors.site: 45 W. 111th St.; Greater Roseland healthcare institution
anchors.evidenceScale: Hospital materials describe RCH as serving Greater Roseland and nearby communities since 1924; public profiles list a nonprofit hospital at 45 W. 111th St. with 134 staffed beds in one profile and 501-1,000 employees in LinkedIn.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Hospital payroll; local healthcare access; patient/visitor traffic; safety-net care; healthcare workforce; induced spending
anchors.rationale: A major service-retention anchor in Greater Roseland. It creates direct health jobs while preventing residents from leaving the area for essential care.
anchors.validationNeeded: Reconcile staff counts across sources, verify current service lines, patient volume, and local hiring/procurement metrics.

anchors.name: SC Johnson / Method South Side Soapbox
anchors.evidenceScale: Pullman Park factory houses manufacturing/bottling and serves as a distribution center; CNI notes additional SC Johnson space. | 150,000 SF plant + additional 400,000 SF facility; current headcount needs validation.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Direct payroll; manufacturing career pathways; vendor/logistics spend; brownfield reuse
anchors.rationale: Strong real-economy anchor because it combines production, distribution, and adaptive reuse on former industrial land. Local impact depends on local hiring and supplier localization.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current headcount, local workforce share, and South Side vendor spend.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Corporate ownership and regional supply chains can leak value outside Pullman without localized procurement.

anchors.name: Amazon Fulfillment Center / Pullman Park logistics cluster
anchors.evidenceScale: CNI identifies Amazon’s Pullman facility with 150,000 SF and 200–300 new jobs. | 150,000 SF; 200–300 jobs cited.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Direct jobs; logistics operations; site activation
anchors.rationale: Grounds the multiplier in job creation and Pullman Park industrial reuse, but local retention may be lower due corporate/regional leakage.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current facility status, employment, wage quality, turnover, and commute patterns.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Large logistics facilities can generate jobs but limited foot traffic and potentially high leakage.

anchors.name: Illinois International Port District / Iroquois Landing freight system
anchors.type: Freight, logistics, and industrial infrastructure anchor
anchors.evidenceScale: IIPD reports rail infrastructure connecting to six of seven North American Class I railroads. | Regional port/freight system; site employment not publicly clear.
anchors.multiplierChannels: B2B freight; logistics; industrial supplier demand
anchors.rationale: Clearest economic anchor tied to South Deering’s industrial geography. Multiplier is mostly indirect freight, warehousing, maintenance, trucking, and supplier activity.
anchors.validationNeeded: Map port assets to community boundaries and estimate tenants, employment, trucking firms, and contracts.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Regional footprint means value may be captured outside South Deering without local workforce/vendor linkages.

anchors.name: Big Marsh Park / Ford Calumet Environmental Center
anchors.evidenceScale: Chicago Park District identifies Big Marsh/Ford Calumet Environmental Center as a major Southeast Side park and system anchor. | Large recreation/civic facility; employment modest, community benefit strong.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Visitor draw; environmental remediation; youth/outdoor programming
anchors.rationale: Converts industrial land into community benefit, recreation, events, and local identity. Multiplier is foot-traffic/community-benefit rather than payroll-heavy.
anchors.validationNeeded: Quantify annual visitors, events, local vendor contracts, and links to Southeast Side businesses.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Visitor spending may leak if adjacent local businesses cannot capture it.

anchors.name: East Side Chamber / Calumet Avenue–95th Street local business corridor
anchors.type: Local business ecosystem + destination retail anchor
anchors.evidenceScale: East Side Chamber supports businesses; Calumet Fisheries is a destination food business. | Cluster/corridor; no single large employment count.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Local retail retention; corridor foot traffic; visitor food spending
anchors.rationale: Because East Side lacks one obvious dominant private employer, local-retention multiplier may come from independent businesses and corridors.
anchors.validationNeeded: Use business licenses, LODES, chamber membership, and corridor checks to identify largest employers.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Corridor anchors need field validation and are not a single-company employment estimate.

anchors.name: Chicago Skyway / Skyway Concession Company
anchors.evidenceScale: Skyway operating presence is at/near 8801 S. Anthony Ave. | Infrastructure operator; public employment data limited.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Direct operations jobs; maintenance contracts; transportation access
anchors.rationale: Site-specific infrastructure anchor, with local impact likely coming through operations, maintenance procurement, and access benefits.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate headcount, contractor/vendor spend, and resident job access.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Toll-road revenue/ownership structures can leak value outside the community.

anchors.name: West Pullman Industrial Center / 119th Street industrial redevelopment
anchors.evidenceScale: City/JLL evidence describes large West Pullman industrial project around 119th Street and 413,400 SF industrial center. | 413,400 SF industrial center; up to 200 jobs cited for related project.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Direct jobs; construction/site activation; logistics/vendor demand
anchors.rationale: Concrete job-producing industrial anchor with direct and indirect potential if workforce pipelines and supplier contracts are localized.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate occupancy, tenants, headcount, hiring geography, and community-benefit terms.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Pipeline/real-estate marketed employment should be separated from current operating payroll.

anchors.name: 119th & Halsted retail/service node / Halsted Plaza
anchors.evidenceScale: Halsted Plaza at 801–837 W. 119th is a high-traffic retail/service center. | Retail/service center; tenant employment requires validation.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Service-gap closure; local shopping retention; foot traffic
anchors.rationale: Directly affects leakage by keeping everyday retail and service spending inside West Pullman if tenant mix fits local needs.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate tenant mix, sales leakage, vacancy, local ownership, and resident use.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Real-estate listing should be verified with parcel, license, and field data.

anchors.name: Altgeld-Murray Homes / People for Community Recovery civic-health ecosystem
anchors.type: Housing, environmental justice, and community service anchor
anchors.evidenceScale: Altgeld-Murray is a major Riverdale public-housing community; PCR is rooted in Altgeld Gardens. | Large residential/civic anchor; employment scale indirect/modest.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Service-gap closure; community wealth; environmental remediation
anchors.rationale: Captures civic infrastructure, housing stability, organizing, and potential service delivery in a community where leakage and environmental burden are core issues.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate onsite provider employment, capital projects, EJ center status, and resident procurement opportunities.
anchors.leakageCaveat: High social impact does not automatically equal high dollar multiplier; budgets need validation.

anchors.name: MWRD Calumet Water Reclamation Plant
anchors.evidenceScale: MWRD says Calumet WRP is one of seven wastewater treatment facilities serving Chicago and 128 Cook County communities. | Major public infrastructure facility at/near 400 E. 130th; headcount not public.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Public-sector jobs; infrastructure contracting; environmental services
anchors.rationale: Major real asset anchoring Riverdale’s infrastructure economy. Multiplier is procurement- and operations-heavy, not retail-heavy.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate facility employment, capital-improvement pipeline, contracted vendors, and boundary placement.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Regional utility infrastructure serves a large area; local retention may be small without local hiring/contracting.

anchors.name: Ford Chicago Assembly Plant
anchors.evidenceScale: Ford’s Chicago Assembly Plant is the strongest manufacturing employment anchor in/near Hegewisch. | Major auto assembly facility; current headcount should be validated.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Direct payroll; supplier demand; skilled manufacturing careers
anchors.rationale: One of the clearest company-level multipliers in the batch. It supports direct jobs and a supplier ecosystem.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current headcount, wage levels, union/workforce pathways, and local supplier base.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Footprint crosses neighborhood/city/suburban boundaries; do not attribute all regional impact to Hegewisch.

anchors.name: Commerce Park Chicago / Ford pre-assembly and supplier cluster
anchors.evidenceScale: Commerce Park is a former Republic Steel redevelopment; CBS reported a 360,000 SF Ford pre-assembly plant. | 360,000 SF Ford pre-assembly plant; larger redevelopment referenced.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Industrial site activation; supplier chain; direct jobs
anchors.rationale: Turns long-vacant industrial land into an auto-adjacent production/logistics platform and gives Hegewisch another multiplier channel.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate tenants, employment, local hiring agreements, and procurement/community-benefit terms.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Avoid double-counting benefits already tied to Ford Assembly Plant.

anchors.name: Midway Airport / Midway Partnership concessions workforce
anchors.type: Airport employment, hospitality, and visitor-spending anchor
anchors.evidenceScale: Midway Partnership says it has hired more than 1,100 people since 2017, largely from local neighborhoods. | Airport-wide employment ecosystem; concessions hiring signal >1,100 since 2017.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Direct jobs; traveler spending; concessions procurement; local hiring
anchors.rationale: Dominant economic engine touching Garfield Ridge through payroll, travel spending, concessions, logistics, and small-business opportunities.
anchors.validationNeeded: Separate Garfield Ridge from Clearing/West Lawn/West Elsdon impacts; validate resident hiring and tenant/vendor ownership.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Airport impact crosses several Southwest Side communities, so do not allocate all activity to Garfield Ridge.

anchors.name: Midway Industrial Corridor TIF / Midway Chamber business ecosystem
anchors.evidenceScale: City TIF page identifies 384-acre Midway Industrial Corridor TIF; chamber supports nearby business communities. | 384-acre TIF district plus chamber ecosystem; jobs require project validation.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Industrial retention; job-creating rehab/new construction; small-business support
anchors.rationale: Captures non-airport business base: industrial retention, small-business networks, and corridor stability.
anchors.validationNeeded: Identify active TIF projects, license clusters, and top employers within Garfield Ridge boundaries.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Corridor ecosystem is real but less precise than a named firm.

anchors.name: Curie Metropolitan High School
anchors.evidenceScale: CPS identifies Curie at 4959 S. Archer Ave. | Large public high school; staffing/enrollment to validate.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Public payroll; student/family foot traffic; workforce pipeline
anchors.rationale: High-confidence civic anchor creating daily population flow, family spending, public payroll, and workforce-development value.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate enrollment, staff count, vendor contracts, and employer partnerships.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Long-term workforce effects are hard to translate into immediate dollar multipliers.

anchors.name: Archer/Pulaski industrial and small-business corridor
anchors.evidenceScale: Chamber describes diverse commercial base, small businesses, and manufacturing district context near Midway. | Corridor/cluster; not one employer.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Industrial retention; local vendor network; corridor foot traffic
anchors.rationale: Multiplier is likely distributed across small manufacturers, services, and Midway-adjacent businesses.
anchors.validationNeeded: Use business license and LODES data to identify largest employers by block/industry.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Chamber geography may extend beyond Archer Heights.

anchors.name: Greater Chicago Food Depository
anchors.type: Food security, workforce training, and nonprofit logistics anchor
anchors.evidenceScale: Food Depository is a regional food bank; BPNC resource guide references job training in food, warehouse, and supply-chain roles. | Large nonprofit/logistics operation; exact Brighton Park employment to validate.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Nonprofit jobs; food distribution; paid training; supply-chain workforce
anchors.rationale: Powerful anchor combining logistics, workforce training, food access, and service delivery.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate site employment, training completions, participant geography, and procurement policies.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Regional nonprofit impact is broad; allocate only a portion to Brighton Park.

anchors.name: Esperanza Health Centers — Brighton Park campus
anchors.evidenceScale: Esperanza identifies the Brighton Park health campus; Mortenson describes a 43,500 SF clinic serving the surrounding community. | 43,500 SF new clinic plus campus operations; employment to validate.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Healthcare jobs; service-gap closure; patient traffic
anchors.rationale: Grounded neighborhood health anchor with high service-gap closure, community trust, and workforce relevance.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate staff count, patient volumes by ZIP/community area, local hiring, and partnerships.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Measure through access, jobs, avoided travel leakage, and patient/community benefits—not only revenue.

anchors.name: Central Manufacturing District / McKinley Park industrial base
anchors.type: Industrial corridor and legacy manufacturing anchor
anchors.evidenceScale: Neighborhood economic sources describe McKinley Park as an important manufacturing/industrial center. | Industrial district/cluster; company-level employment needs validation.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Industrial retention; B2B procurement; workforce pathways
anchors.rationale: Strongest economic multiplier is industrial land and employer cluster; identify firms/vendors rather than assume one employer.
anchors.validationNeeded: Use LODES, business licenses, and industrial tenant maps to identify top operating employers.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Industrial corridors create B2B value but can also create externalities.

anchors.name: McKinley Park Development Council / neighborhood commercial-civic corridor
anchors.evidenceScale: MPDC supports neighborhood organizing and economic/civic coordination; MAT Asphalt included as a risk note. | Civic/business ecosystem; no single large employment count.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Small-business support; corridor activation; community reinvestment
anchors.rationale: Included to balance industrial jobs with quality of life and locally acceptable project development.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate MPDC/member business base, vacancies, active projects, and industrial externalities.
anchors.leakageCaveat: MAT Asphalt may be economically significant but carries environmental/community concern flags.

anchors.name: Bridgeport Art Center
anchors.type: Creative economy, events, and adaptive-reuse anchor
anchors.evidenceScale: Bridgeport Art Center describes a multidisciplinary creative home at 1200 W. 35th Street. | Creative/event building; tenant employment and visitors require validation.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Creative jobs; events; visitor spending; adaptive reuse
anchors.rationale: Creative-industry buildings pull visitors and support artists, events, caterers, fabricators, and local businesses.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate tenants, event volumes, local vendor/catering spend, and spillover to 35th Street businesses.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Creative anchors drive foot traffic but not necessarily large payroll.

anchors.name: Zhou B Art Center / Bridgeport arts corridor
anchors.type: Arts, events, and cultural placemaking anchor
anchors.evidenceScale: Zhou B Art Center supports resident artists, exhibitions, and events. | Resident artists/events; exact jobs/revenue not public.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Arts/culture foot traffic; independent vendors; community identity
anchors.rationale: Adds a second arts-led multiplier channel and creates a creative cluster rather than isolated assets.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate occupancy, event frequency, visitor counts, vendors, and nearby spending capture.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Arts impacts may be unevenly retained if visitors do not shop locally.

anchors.name: Stockyards Industrial Corridor / Back of the Yards LIRI
anchors.evidenceScale: City says Stockyards TIF fosters commercial and industrial viability; BYNC is a City-contracted LIRI agency. | Large industrial corridor; direct employment requires firm-level validation.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Industrial retention; vendor development; B2B procurement
anchors.rationale: Top multiplier is the modern industrial legacy: the Stockyards/Back of the Yards employer base supported by business-retention infrastructure.
anchors.validationNeeded: Identify top employers/vendors, LIRI-supported businesses, hiring geography, and procurement categories.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Corridor spans a large geography; avoid double-counting adjacent areas.

anchors.name: Testa Produce / food distribution and sustainable logistics cluster
anchors.type: Food distribution, cold storage, and logistics anchor
anchors.evidenceScale: Facility profile describes a LEED-NC Platinum refrigerated distribution facility with office, freezer, cooler, warehouse, and docks. | 12.86-acre facility; cold storage/warehouse; employment to validate.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Food distribution jobs; truck logistics; supplier spend
anchors.rationale: Concrete company-level anchor inside New City’s food/industrial economy.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current employment, customer/vendor geography, and local hiring pathways.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Regional value may leak unless workforce and vendors are local.

anchors.name: Pulaski/Archer commercial corridor and Midway-adjacent spillover
anchors.type: Commercial corridor and airport-adjacent service anchor
anchors.evidenceScale: West Elsdon is near Midway; Midway Chamber and Southwest business networks cover this geography. | Corridor/cluster; firm-level employment to validate.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Corridor retail; services; airport-adjacent spending
anchors.rationale: Economic potential is tied to everyday retail/service retention plus Midway spillover, not one dominant employer.
anchors.validationNeeded: Use licenses and field checks along Pulaski, Archer, 55th/59th to identify largest employers and leakage gaps.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Airport spillover should not be double-counted with Garfield Ridge/Clearing.

anchors.name: John F. Kennedy High School
anchors.evidenceScale: CPS identifies Kennedy High School at 6325 W. 56th Street; WTTW notes Midway-adjacent context. | Large public high school; current enrollment/staffing to validate.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Public payroll; student/family activity; workforce pipeline
anchors.rationale: Most grounded community anchor in West Elsdon; steady local effects from family activity and public payroll.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate enrollment, staff count, local partnerships, and procurement.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Education impacts are long-term and should not be equated to private-sector payroll.

anchors.name: Southwest Collective / NBDC and Gage Park small-business corridors
anchors.evidenceScale: Southwest Collective’s NBDC serves Gage Park and nearby Southwest Side communities. | Small-business/corridor ecosystem; no single large employer.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Small-business retention; entrepreneurship; corridor activation
anchors.rationale: Near-term multiplier likely comes from strengthening small businesses and corridors rather than waiting on one large employer.
anchors.validationNeeded: Map NBDC clients, license clusters, vacancies, and procurement opportunities.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Service-provider geography crosses communities; Gage Park-specific outcomes need validation.

anchors.name: Former Central Steel & Wire / Amazon 3000 W. 51st industrial site
anchors.evidenceScale: PitchBook identifies Central Steel & Wire’s 70-acre Gage Park plant and Amazon as acquirer; state record identifies Amazon.com Services LLC at same address. | 70-acre site; operating status and jobs require validation.
anchors.multiplierChannels: Industrial site activation; logistics/construction; potential direct jobs
anchors.rationale: Major grounded site, but treat as pipeline/uncertain until operating status, employment, approvals, and community impacts are verified.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate whether Amazon is actively operating, job count, traffic/environmental impacts, community benefits, and status.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Do not count projected jobs as realized multiplier until active operations and employment are confirmed.

anchors.name: Belt Railway Company of Chicago / Clearing Yard
anchors.evidenceScale: Largest intermediate switching terminal railroad in the U.S.; approximately 450 employees; Clearing Yard spans roughly 786 acres with 250+ miles of track. | ~450 employees; 786-acre rail yard; regional freight-switching infrastructure
anchors.multiplierChannels: Direct payroll; freight logistics; B2B contracting; industrial land retention
anchors.rationale: This is the clearest company-level anchor in Clearing. It creates direct payroll and B2B demand through rail operations, maintenance, switching, and freight-related services, though much supplier spend is likely regional/national.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm current site employment, resident hiring share, and Chicago/local vendor spend.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Rail freight value is regional by design; neighborhood-retained impact depends on worker residence, local contractors, and nearby supporting firms.

anchors.name: Clearing Industrial District / Midway-adjacent industrial ecosystem
anchors.evidenceScale: Clearing has a long-standing industrial district tied to freight, warehousing, and Midway-adjacent logistics activity. | Industrial corridor/ecosystem; establishment-level employment needs validation
anchors.multiplierChannels: B2B procurement; light industrial jobs; logistics; property activation
anchors.rationale: The second multiplier is best treated as an industrial cluster rather than one named company. The local upside is in mapping employers, suppliers, truck services, repair, maintenance, and warehousing users that retain industrial jobs within the community area.
anchors.validationNeeded: Use LODES, city business licenses, parcel data, and field checks to identify the top operating establishments.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Because this is a cluster anchor, avoid double-counting with Belt Railway and nearby Midway/O'Hare logistics flows.

anchors.name: Richard J. Daley College / MTEC
anchors.evidenceScale: City Colleges anchor at 7500 S. Pulaski Road; major education facility with manufacturing, health, business, IT, and transfer pathways. | 486,156 sq. ft. campus; major community college / workforce training facility
anchors.multiplierChannels: Workforce training; student spending; local hiring; vendor spend; service-gap closure
anchors.rationale: Daley College is the strongest grounded anchor because it links residents to credentials, manufacturing and technical training, employer pipelines, and student/staff activity. Its multiplier is strongest through workforce formation and neighborhood-facing services.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate program-level employer partnerships, graduation/job placement data, and student origin by ZIP/community area.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Students and staff may come from across the Southwest Side, so site impact should be separated from broader district impact.

anchors.name: Ford City Mall / Ford City redevelopment site
anchors.evidenceScale: Major enclosed Southwest Side mall in West Lawn with large retail square footage and several anchors; current operating status and redevelopment trajectory require validation. | ~1.26 million sq. ft. retail property profile; large regional retail site
anchors.multiplierChannels: Retail jobs; customer foot traffic; redevelopment; leakage capture
anchors.rationale: Ford City is a large local-spending capture site, but its multiplier should be treated carefully because malls can have leakage through national chains and because operating/redevelopment status may change quickly.
anchors.validationNeeded: Confirm current tenant roster, operating status, employment, ownership plan, vacancy, and redevelopment pipeline.
anchors.leakageCaveat: National retail chains leak profits and procurement outside the neighborhood; redevelopment may have greater future impact than current operations.

anchors.name: Holy Cross Hospital / Sinai Chicago
anchors.evidenceScale: Sinai Chicago's Holy Cross Hospital is a 264-licensed-bed community hospital at 2701 W. 68th Street. | 264 licensed beds; community hospital serving Chicago Lawn and Southwest Side
anchors.multiplierChannels: Direct payroll; healthcare service retention; procurement; patient/family foot traffic
anchors.rationale: Holy Cross is the strongest single anchor because healthcare payroll is labor-intensive and the hospital keeps patients, workers, and healthcare spending in or near the neighborhood.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current employment, procurement, resident hiring, and patient-origin data.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Hospital catchment extends beyond Chicago Lawn; local impact should distinguish patient service area from community-area-retained impact.

anchors.name: Greater Southwest Development Corporation / 63rd Street + housing corridor ecosystem
anchors.evidenceScale: GSDC works on neighborhood development, local business support, senior housing, corridor activity, and Southwest Side reinvestment. | Community development corporation; ~250 senior housing units managed; 63rd Street corridor programming
anchors.multiplierChannels: Small business support; housing retention; corridor foot traffic; community reinvestment
anchors.rationale: GSDC is not the largest employer, but it is a strong local-retention anchor because it builds neighborhood capacity, supports local merchants, and helps address commercial leakage and housing stability.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate direct staff size, corridor business outcomes, financing leveraged, and local vendor participation.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Impact is distributed across multiple Southwest Side neighborhoods; isolate Chicago Lawn-specific outcomes where possible.

anchors.name: Growing Home Urban Farm & Workforce Development
anchors.evidenceScale: USDA-certified organic urban farm and workforce development nonprofit social enterprise in Englewood/West Englewood; paid training and healthy-food access. | Urban farm, training center, planned expansion with commercial kitchen / farm store elements
anchors.multiplierChannels: Paid workforce training; fresh food access; local procurement; vacant land reuse
anchors.rationale: Growing Home is a high-grounding anchor despite smaller employment scale because it links food access, paid training, vacant-land activation, and community reinvestment in a neighborhood with high leakage.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current participant counts, job-placement rates, farm/store revenue, and local supplier/customer geography.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Some operations and program benefits may cross the Englewood/West Englewood boundary.

anchors.name: Lindblom Math and Science Academy
anchors.evidenceScale: Selective enrollment high school at 6130 S. Wolcott with strong STEM identity and broad student/family activity. | Large CPS high school; STEM and college-preparatory institutional anchor
anchors.multiplierChannels: Education; youth talent pipeline; daily student/family activity; civic presence
anchors.rationale: Lindblom is not a procurement-heavy anchor, but it is a stable public institution that brings staff, students, families, and long-term talent development into West Englewood.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current enrollment, staff count, community partnerships, and local vendor/career pathway linkages.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Selective enrollment draws students from across Chicago, so resident-specific benefit should not be assumed without data.

anchors.name: St. Bernard Hospital / Ambulatory Care Center
anchors.evidenceScale: Long-standing Englewood hospital with community development role and outpatient/ambulatory services that reduce healthcare leakage. | Hospital, ambulatory care, pharmacy/clinics, Bernard Place community development activity
anchors.multiplierChannels: Healthcare payroll; local service retention; procurement; community development
anchors.rationale: St. Bernard is a top Englewood anchor because it combines direct healthcare employment, essential service-gap closure, patient traffic, and explicit community-development activity.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current employment, service volumes, local hiring, vendor spend, and Bernard Place outcomes.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Hospital service area crosses neighborhood boundaries; focus on Englewood resident access and local employment where possible.

anchors.name: Kennedy-King College / Washburne Culinary Institute
anchors.evidenceScale: City Colleges campus at 6301 S. Halsted with career, construction, culinary, and academic pathways. | Major community college campus; includes workforce-oriented divisions such as Washburne Culinary Institute and Dawson Technical Institute
anchors.multiplierChannels: Workforce training; student spending; local hiring; employer pipeline; foot traffic
anchors.rationale: Kennedy-King is a powerful anchor because it converts public education investment into local workforce pathways and corridor activity along Halsted.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate campus employment, enrollment by community area, employer partnerships, placement outcomes, and local procurement.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Regional students may benefit beyond Englewood; neighborhood retention depends on local student/resident participation and nearby business capture.

anchors.name: Gary Comer Youth Center / Comer Education Campus
anchors.evidenceScale: Youth-serving anchor in Greater Grand Crossing with a campus that includes an 80,000 sq. ft. youth center and associated education assets. | 13.5-acre campus; 80,000 sq. ft. youth center; education/youth-development cluster
anchors.multiplierChannels: Youth development; education; community programming; local employment; reinvestment
anchors.rationale: Gary Comer is the most grounded local-impact anchor because it combines youth development, education, campus investment, and community-serving programming in Greater Grand Crossing.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current employment, participant counts, local hiring, procurement, and school/community partnership outcomes.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Some benefits are long-term human-capital gains rather than immediate dollar recirculation.

anchors.name: 75th Street / Renaissance Row / Greater Stony Island commercial corridor
anchors.evidenceScale: 75th Street / Renaissance Row is a central neighborhood commercial district, supported by Greater Stony Island planning context. | Corridor ecosystem; establishment-level employer and sales data needs validation
anchors.multiplierChannels: Small business retention; foot traffic; local vendor loops; corridor activation
anchors.rationale: The second anchor is a corridor rather than one company. Its multiplier comes from independent merchants, local services, and leakage capture along 75th and nearby commercial nodes.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current tenant mix, sales leakage, vacancy, employment, and local ownership share.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Corridor impact is distributed and may overlap with Chatham/South Shore/Avalon Park trade areas.

anchors.name: William J. Bogan High School / Bogan Park node
anchors.evidenceScale: Bogan High School at 3939 W. 79th Street offers IB, career pathways, entrepreneurship/accounting, and dual enrollment connections. | CPS high school / civic node on 79th Street
anchors.multiplierChannels: Education; youth pipeline; family traffic; civic activity; corridor presence
anchors.rationale: Bogan is a stable anchor in a largely residential community area, creating daily institutional activity, family traffic, and pathways that can connect youth to local employment.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current enrollment, staff count, CTE outcomes, dual-enrollment participation, and local partnerships.
anchors.leakageCaveat: School impact is more human-capital than immediate B2B spending; student catchment may extend beyond Ashburn.

anchors.name: Greater Ashburn Development Association / 79th-Cicero-Western corridor network
anchors.evidenceScale: GADA and CMAP planning identify redevelopment and safety priorities along major Ashburn corridors including 79th, Cicero, and Western. | Community development/corridor network; specific business-level impacts need validation
anchors.multiplierChannels: Corridor activation; small business support; local procurement; pedestrian safety and access
anchors.rationale: Because Ashburn lacks one obvious dominant employer, the second multiplier is best grounded in corridor organization and local-business ecosystem building.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate active membership, corridor business counts, vacancy, local ownership, foot traffic, and investments delivered.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Corridor network spans multiple commercial nodes and may capture spending from neighboring communities.

anchors.name: Auburn Gresham Healthy Lifestyle Hub / GAGDC
anchors.type: Health, service, and community wealth anchor
anchors.evidenceScale: Repurposed long-vacant building at 839 W. 79th providing healthcare, banking, pharmacy, food access, training, and community services. | Healthy Lifestyle Hub; UI Health clinic; banking/pharmacy/food access; multi-service redevelopment
anchors.multiplierChannels: Service-gap closure; healthcare access; local hiring; corridor foot traffic; reinvestment
anchors.rationale: This is one of the strongest local-retention anchors in the final batches because it directly plugs multiple leakage points: healthcare, banking, pharmacy, food, internet access, training, and 79th Street foot traffic.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate tenant employment, patient visits, local hiring, small-business spend, and ongoing operating performance.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Some services draw from surrounding South Side neighborhoods; neighborhood-retained impact depends on Auburn Gresham user share.

anchors.name: St. Sabina Employment Resource Center
anchors.evidenceScale: Full-service employment center serving Auburn Gresham/Englewood residents with job matching, training, resume support, and workforce services. | Workforce center; faith/community network; job fairs and training services
anchors.multiplierChannels: Resident hiring; job placement; training; community trust; employer connections
anchors.rationale: The ERC scores highly because its impact is not just institutional presence; it directly connects residents to jobs, increasing induced local wage spending if placements remain accessible and stable.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate annual placement outcomes, wage levels, employer retention, and share of participants from Auburn Gresham.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Employment impacts may occur outside the neighborhood; the local multiplier depends on whether resident wages are spent locally.

anchors.name: Mercy Circle
anchors.evidenceScale: Senior living community in Beverly with assisted living, skilled nursing, and continuing-care functions. | Senior living campus at 3659 W. 99th Street; healthcare-adjacent service employment
anchors.multiplierChannels: Direct care jobs; service retention; healthcare-adjacent procurement; family visits
anchors.rationale: Mercy Circle is the most company/institution-like anchor in Beverly because senior living is labor-intensive, locally rooted, and service-retention oriented.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current staff count, resident count, local hiring, and vendor/procurement geography.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Spending from residents and families may be captured by nearby Beverly/Morgan Park corridors or leak to regional providers.

anchors.name: 95th Street Business Association / Beverly commercial corridor
anchors.evidenceScale: Long-running merchant association supporting 95th Street businesses, farmers market activity, beautification, and local economic development. | Commercial corridor association; independent business ecosystem
anchors.multiplierChannels: Small-business retention; local vendor loops; foot traffic; events; leakage capture
anchors.rationale: The second anchor is a corridor ecosystem. Its multiplier comes from local ownership, customer capture, and cross-spending among restaurants, retail, services, events, and nearby civic anchors.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current member count, sales/vacancy data, local ownership share, and corridor foot traffic.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Corridor overlaps with Morgan Park/Beverly trade areas; impacts should be attributed carefully.

anchors.name: Endeleo Institute / Trinity United Church of Christ network
anchors.evidenceScale: Endeleo combines health, education, community development, food access, capital access, job creation, and 95th Street corridor work from Washington Heights. | Faith-rooted community development institution tied to 95th Street corridor strategy
anchors.multiplierChannels: Community reinvestment; resident hiring; food access; corridor activation; service-gap closure
anchors.rationale: Endeleo is the strongest grounded anchor because it intentionally turns institutional trust into local economic development, food access, health, and job-creation activity.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current program budgets, jobs created, local vendor participation, business launches, and corridor activation outcomes.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Impact is neighborhood-rooted but can span Washington Heights, Roseland, and broader Far South Side networks.

anchors.name: 95th Street Corridor Plan / Washington Heights commercial corridor
anchors.evidenceScale: City 95th Street corridor planning covers Roseland and a portion of Washington Heights, with commercial activation and service-access opportunities. | Commercial corridor / redevelopment planning area; business-level impacts need validation
anchors.multiplierChannels: Foot traffic; local business retention; storefront activation; food and service access
anchors.rationale: The second anchor is a redevelopment corridor, not a single firm. It is important because 95th Street can convert public planning and storefront activation into merchant activity and resident spending capture.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate project pipeline, funded storefronts, active businesses, vacancy, foot traffic, and Washington Heights-specific boundaries.
anchors.leakageCaveat: The city plan is cross-boundary; separate Washington Heights gains from Roseland corridor outcomes.

anchors.name: Saint Xavier University
anchors.evidenceScale: Saint Xavier University is located in Mount Greenwood at 3700 W. 103rd Street and has a sizable campus footprint. | University campus; roughly 74-acre / 620,000 sq. ft. campus profile
anchors.multiplierChannels: Payroll; student spending; workforce pathways; vendor demand; civic activity
anchors.rationale: SXU is the clear primary anchor because it combines institutional payroll, student/staff activity, procurement, and neighborhood-facing education functions.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate current employment, student enrollment, local procurement, community partnerships, and resident attendance.
anchors.leakageCaveat: University activity extends beyond Mount Greenwood; local retention depends on nearby business capture and local hiring.

anchors.name: Chicago High School for Agricultural Sciences
anchors.evidenceScale: Public high school with a large land lab and agriculture-focused college/career curriculum in Mount Greenwood. | 72-acre land lab / working-farm educational asset; CTE and college/career curriculum
anchors.multiplierChannels: CTE workforce pipeline; local food/agriculture learning; civic identity; family traffic
anchors.rationale: CHSAS is a distinctive local anchor because it connects education, agriculture, workforce preparation, and land-based learning in a way few Chicago neighborhoods can replicate.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate enrollment, staff count, employer partnerships, farm/food procurement, and alumni job outcomes.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Economic impact is partly long-term talent development; direct spending footprint is likely smaller than SXU.

anchors.name: Smith Village
anchors.evidenceScale: Long-standing senior living community in southwest Chicago with continuum-of-care functions. | Senior living/care campus at 2320 W. 113th Place; long-standing local institution
anchors.multiplierChannels: Care jobs; service retention; local procurement; family visits
anchors.rationale: Smith Village is the most grounded employer/service anchor because senior care is labor-intensive, stable, and locally embedded.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate staff count, resident count, local hiring, and vendor spend.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Resident/family spending may be captured by both Morgan Park and Beverly corridors.

anchors.name: Morgan Park Beverly Hills Business Association / local commercial districts
anchors.evidenceScale: Business association representing 400+ Beverly/Morgan Park businesses and supporting local entrepreneurs/commercial districts. | 400+ business network across Beverly/Morgan Park; corridor and entrepreneur support
anchors.multiplierChannels: Small-business retention; local vendor loops; corridor foot traffic; entrepreneurship
anchors.rationale: This is the strongest second anchor because the multiplier is distributed across many local businesses rather than one employer. It helps reveal resident-spending capture and local ownership.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate Morgan Park-specific membership, business employment, local ownership, and foot traffic.
anchors.leakageCaveat: The association spans Beverly and Morgan Park, so community-area attribution needs careful separation.

anchors.name: O'Hare International Airport / Chicago Department of Aviation
anchors.type: Global airport and aviation employment anchor
anchors.evidenceScale: O'Hare economic impact reporting identifies massive on-airport activity, jobs, visitor spending, and labor income tied to the airport. | $22.1B on-airport activity; 217,660 jobs supported; $15B visitor spending; major airport/cargo gateway
anchors.multiplierChannels: Direct payroll; visitor spending; cargo/logistics; procurement; hospitality; regional employment
anchors.rationale: O'Hare is the strongest anchor in the entire final batch. It imports external dollars, supports aviation/logistics employment, and creates demand across ground transport, hotels, food service, cargo, maintenance, construction, and professional services.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate neighborhood-resident employment, local vendor share, and O'Hare community-area attribution distinct from regional airport impact.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Most airport value is regional/metropolitan, not retained in the O'Hare community area; use neighborhood retention assumptions cautiously.

anchors.name: O'Hare cargo, logistics, hotel, and airport-services ecosystem
anchors.evidenceScale: O'Hare includes a large cargo ecosystem, airside and landside cargo facilities, and airport-adjacent service businesses. | ~2M sq. ft. airside cargo plus additional landside cargo; expanding cargo/logistics capacity
anchors.multiplierChannels: Cargo handling; logistics jobs; maintenance; hotel/restaurant demand; supplier spend
anchors.rationale: This is separated from the airport authority anchor to show the second-level economic engine: cargo handlers, freight forwarders, hotels, food service, maintenance, and airport-adjacent businesses.
anchors.validationNeeded: Avoid double-counting with airport totals; validate employer-level cargo/logistics counts and local hiring.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Highly regional supply chains create leakage; neighborhood retention depends on nearby business capture and resident employment.

anchors.name: Loyola University Chicago Lake Shore Campus
anchors.evidenceScale: Loyola's Lake Shore Campus sits in Edgewater and Rogers Park, creating student/staff activity, procurement, and institutional spillovers. | Major university campus; cross-boundary Lake Shore Campus footprint
anchors.multiplierChannels: Payroll; student spending; procurement; visitor traffic; talent pipeline
anchors.rationale: Loyola is the strongest Edgewater/Rogers Park institutional anchor. The local multiplier depends on how much student, staff, visitor, and procurement spending is captured by Edgewater businesses.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate Edgewater-specific spending, employee residence, vendor spend, and campus boundary attribution.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Campus crosses Rogers Park/Edgewater dynamics; avoid double-counting with Batch 1 Rogers Park analysis.

anchors.name: Edgewater + Andersonville independent business ecosystem
anchors.evidenceScale: Edgewater Chamber and Andersonville Chamber support independent businesses, small-business services, marketing, advocacy, and local commercial activity. | Chamber / NBDC / independent business corridor network
anchors.multiplierChannels: Independent business retention; local vendor loops; foot traffic; entrepreneurship; service access
anchors.rationale: The second anchor is the independent-business ecosystem across Broadway, Clark/Andersonville, and related Edgewater corridors. This is where local ownership and consumer-spending retention can produce higher neighborhood multipliers.
anchors.validationNeeded: Validate Edgewater-specific member count, local ownership share, sales leakage, vacancy, and visitor/resident spending.
anchors.leakageCaveat: Andersonville overlaps community-area perceptions and may spill into Uptown; boundaries need to be explicit.
